addons.name: Project Halo
addons.author: nyannoying
addons.summary: The 2026 F1 world feed's onboard halo for 2026, 2025 and F2 cars, an animated broadcast-style timing tower, the Race Control banner and an optional G-force meter, drawn by F1 25's own HUD. Read from the game itself: no UDP telemetry, no companion app.
addons.description:
## The 2026 world feed's halo, timing tower and broadcast cards, in the game's own HUD

Project Halo puts the onboard halo graphic from the 2026 F1 world feed in place of the dial of F1 25's 2026, 2025 and F2 cars, an animated, broadcast-style timing tower in place of the Track Position list, and the pit lane timer and the lap times as broadcast cards. The game's own HUD draws all of them, so you move and resize them in HUD customisation like any other element, and they hide when the game hides its HUD.

Project Halo reads the running game itself and changes nothing in it: no UDP telemetry, no companion app, and the game's telemetry settings make no difference.

### Quick start

1. Steam version of F1 25 with the official 2026 Season Pack and Swofty Launcher 1.8.36 or newer. Install Project Halo from the Addon Browser, then start the game.
2. Open HUD customisation (in the settings, or the pause menu during a session) and select the dial, the Track Position list or one of the cards.
3. Move and resize them, then go Back to save. Each HUD layout (practice, qualifying, race) keeps its own position and size.

### What you get

- **The halo:** your speed in km/h and mph, gear and revs, throttle and brake, the battery, Recharge and Deploy, Boost, Overtake and Active Aero, your position and the car ahead, and the next turn's number and direction.
- **Two halo layouts:** Default camera sits on the car's own halo as the default T-cam shows it, even-sided and larger. TV offset is the broadcast's off-centre halo at the bottom of the screen.
- **Halo animations:** a bright streak runs out along both wings when Boost or Overtake comes on, the gear number ticks on every shift, the RPM line turns white near the limiter, the name of the car ahead rolls over when it changes, and the active aero bars turn between their two shapes.
- **Suggested gear:** with the game's assist Manual with suggested gear on, the suggested gear lights up on the gear strip with a small pointer, green for a higher gear and amber for a lower one.
- **2025 and F2 cars:** the same halo with DRS. 2025 cars also show the ERS deploy mode (NONE, MEDIUM, HOTLAP, OVERTAKE), the battery and Recharge and Deploy. F2 cars have no energy parts.
- **Timing tower:** positions, team logos and colours, driver codes, intervals or gaps to the leader, tyres, PIT, Out, DSQ and NC, and a green or red arrow when a car gains or loses a place. Its header shows the lap or the session, and the safety car, virtual safety car, yellow flag, red flag and chequered flag. Practice, qualifying, races, Time Trial, replays, the highlights reel and the spectator view, with up to 30 cars.
- **Tower animations:** when cars change places, their rows slide into their new positions, fast at first and then settling, like the broadcast. The position arrow rides in with its row, and the position number and a new best lap time fade in. Flag cards (yellow flag, VSC, safety car, red flag, chequered flag) slide down out of the header and the rows move down with them; when the flag ends, the card rolls back up and the rows close the gap.
- **Lap times in practice and qualifying:** the leader's best lap and every other car's gap to it. A new personal best flashes green for 2 seconds, a new session best purple. The header shows the session's clock, and in Q1 and Q2 (SQ1 and SQ2 in sprint qualifying) a red hatch marks the cars in the knockout zone.
- **Fastest lap in races:** a purple stopwatch beside the car with the fastest lap.
- **Pit lane timer:** position, team logo, surname, team colour line, IN PIT with the pit lane time, and the stop time under it.
- **Lap time card:** position, team logo, surname and tyre, the running lap time, and S1, S2 and S3 as bars that grow in white and take the game's sector colour. The lap time turns green on a personal best and purple on the session's fastest lap. Best and Previous sit below.
- **Race Control banner:** the game's own race messages, in the style of the broadcast's Race Control banner. At pit entry the whole message is red while you are over the pit limit and green once you are under it.
- **Spectator view:** the halo shows the car you watch, and the tower replaces the spectator board with that car highlighted. The tower follows the Spectator Menu's Gap and Detail options.
- **G-force meter (optional):** the 2026 broadcast's G-force meter in the middle of the halo.

### Requirements

- F1 25 on Steam, build 25251167. After a game update Project Halo stops reading the game until a new version is out: the halo then shows only the values the game gives its own dial (battery, Overtake, Active Aero, your position).
- The official 2026 Season Pack.
- Swofty Launcher 1.8.36 or newer, with Swofty Core 0.1.1 or newer.
- Offline sessions.

### Settings

In ADDON SETTINGS on the home menu (directly under Career, or F9 / R3), or in the launcher.

- **Halo dial**, **Timing tower**, **Race Control banner**, **Pit lane timer**, **Lap time card** and **Pit speed colour** (all On): one switch for every part. Off gives that part of the game's own HUD back. The Timing tower switches at once; the others apply after a restart. Pit speed colour needs the Race Control banner on.
- **Halo layout** (Default camera): Default camera or TV offset.
- **Driver names** (On): your position and name, and the car one place ahead in the session's classification (the car in P2 when you lead), on the left wing. Practice, qualifying and races; not in Time Trial.
- **Turn numbers** (On): the next turn's number and direction, from 220 m before it.
- **G-force meter** (Off): replaces the speed, Boost, Overtake, battery and Recharge and Deploy in the middle of the halo with the G-force meter.
- **Suggested gear** (On): the game's gear suggestion on the halo's gear strip. It shows only while the game's suggested gear assist is on.
- **Halo in 2025 and F2 cars** (On): off, those cars show their own dials.
- For the timing tower: **Tower layout** (Around me, Leaders or Full field), **Tower rows** (5), **Gap mode** (Interval, Leader or Auto), **Auto switch every** (10 s), and switches for the **Tower header**, **Tyres**, **Position arrows**, **Intervals**, **Team logos** and **Highlight my row** (all On).
- **Animations** (On): the tower's and the halo's animations. Off: every change shows at once.
- **Validation log** (Off): writes what the halo and the tower read from the game as CSV (two files, up to 64 MB each per launch) and shows a status line under the tower. Turn it on only to send a log.

### Beta status

- Driven in practice, qualifying and races with 2026, 2025 and F2 cars, in replays and in the spectator view. In the 2026 cars, speed, gear, revs, throttle, brake, the battery, Recharge, Deploy, Boost, Overtake, the car ahead and the turn numbers matched the game's own values in the validation logs.
- The tower's animations were driven in practice, qualifying and races, the flag cards with yellow flags, a VSC, a safety car and a red flag.
- New in 0.2.2 and driven in races: the halo's animations, the Default camera layout, the pit lane timer, the lap time card, the pit speed colours and the tower in the highlights reel.
- New in 0.2.3 and driven: the suggested gear marks.
- **Not confirmed yet:** the suggested gear in 2025 and F2 cars and with the G-force meter, Active Aero, the DRS states of 2025 and F2 cars, the tower in Time Trial, the tower's animations in replays and the spectator view, the spectator view's flag message fix, the G-force meter, the game's own HUD parts coming back with the Halo dial, Pit lane timer or Lap time card switched off, and the cards in practice, qualifying and Time Trial.

### Known issues

- Halo layout Default camera: fitted to a 2026 car in the default T-cam at 16:9. Other cars, other cameras, ultrawide screens and changed camera settings can sit differently: move or resize the halo in HUD customisation, or use TV offset.
- Halo layout Default camera: a halo you already moved in HUD customisation ends up higher and larger. Place it again once.
- Halo layout Default camera: the game's tutorial message and the open MFD can touch the halo.
- The pit window stays the game's own.
- The running lap time shows three decimals; the game gives the HUD no shorter form.
- STOP TIME and PIT LIMIT are in English in every language.
- My Team: your own team's logo stays empty in the tower.
- Time Trial: long driver names in the tower look squeezed.
- Full field with more than 22 cars: the tower can run past the bottom of the screen. Make it smaller in HUD customisation, or use Around me or Leaders.
- With the timing tower on and Track Position switched off in HUD customisation, the game's lap counter stays hidden too. Turn the Timing tower setting off to get it back.
- Depending on the screen resolution, the scaling might be off.

### Good to know

- Animations: when several cars change places within a moment, or your own place changes in Around me, those rows switch at once instead of sliding, so every row always shows its own car. A flag card that replaces another (a yellow flag becoming a VSC) also switches at once.
- Turn numbers follow the official F1 numbering on the 24 standard circuits. On reverse layouts and tracks without an official list, the halo finds the corners itself from the cars' line once a lap is covered and numbers them from the start line: those numbers are its own, not official.
- When a value cannot be read, its part stays empty. Project Halo never shows a made-up value.
- Split screen: the halo hides, because two cars are driven by players.
- Spectating offline needs a spectator addon. The spectator view was tested with Spectator/Broadcast Mode.
- Halo layout Default camera is fitted to a 2026 car in the default T-cam at 16:9. In another camera, move the halo in HUD customisation or pick TV offset.
- Turn the addon off to get the game's own HUD back, or switch off single parts in the settings.

**Something not working?** Turn on Validation log, drive a few laps and send me the log.

**Your log:** the newest halo_*.csv and tower_*.csv in swofty\addons\nick.f1-2026-halo\diag in the F1 25 game folder (zipped), and loader.log in the newest folder of %LOCALAPPDATA%\Swofty\sessions. Post them in a [GitHub issue](https://github.com/nyannoying1337/f1-25-project-halo/issues).

### Source and license

Source and how it works: [GitHub](https://github.com/nyannoying1337/f1-25-project-halo).

This release uses the [Project Halo Attribution License 1.0](https://github.com/nyannoying1337/f1-25-project-halo/blob/main/LICENSE), a custom license. Published mods/projects using substantial parts must credit Project Halo by nyannoying with a link to the project.

Graphics drawn with the Saira typeface (SIL Open Font License 1.1, © 2020 The Saira Project Authors).

Fan-made. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the FIA, Formula 1, EA or Codemasters. Their names and marks belong to their owners.

# Project Halo 0.2.4 beta

Quick fix for the F1 25 update 1.0.145 (Steam). On that version the halo and the timing tower showed no data, because the game's memory layout moved.

### Fixed

- The halo and the timing tower read the game again on F1 25 1.0.145 (Steam). Thanks to faustp6-alt for the fix.

### Known issues

- Not yet tested in game on 1.0.145. If a value looks wrong, switch the part off in the settings and report it.
- This version works only on F1 25 1.0.145 (Steam). On the older game version the halo shows no data.
- Custom team badges: the game's default badge is not recognised on this version.

versions.changelog:
# Project Halo 0.2.4 beta

Quick fix for the F1 25 update 1.0.145 (Steam). On that version the halo and the timing tower showed no data, because the game's memory layout moved.

### Fixed

- The halo and the timing tower read the game again on F1 25 1.0.145 (Steam). Thanks to faustp6-alt for the fix.

### Known issues

- Not yet tested in game on 1.0.145. If a value looks wrong, switch the part off in the settings and report it.
- This version works only on F1 25 1.0.145 (Steam). On the older game version the halo shows no data.
- Custom team badges: the game's default badge is not recognised on this version.

# Project Halo 0.2.3 beta

The halo now shows the game's suggested gear. Players who drive with the gear suggestion assist no longer lose the hint when the halo replaces the game's dial.

## New

- **Suggested gear:** with the game's assist Manual with suggested gear on, the gear the game suggests lights up on the halo's gear strip with a small pointer: green when it is higher than your gear, amber when it is lower. In the right gear, or with the assist off, nothing extra shows. Both halo layouts, 2026, 2025 and F2 cars, also with the G-force meter. The new setting Suggested gear (On) switches it off.

## Known issues

- Suggested gear: a mark shows about 0.15 seconds after the game names a gear, and a gear you just left stays dark for 0.3 seconds.
- Suggested gear: the mark shows and hides at once; it has no animation.
- Suggested gear: no mark in the spectator view.

## Setup

Steam version of F1 25 with the official 2026 Season Pack, and Swofty Launcher 1.8.36 or newer. Install or update Project Halo from the Addon Browser in the launcher, or import the zip there, then start the game.

Full notes: https://github.com/nyannoying1337/f1-25-project-halo/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

# Project Halo 0.2.2 beta

The halo now moves: a streak runs along the wings on Boost and Overtake, the gear number ticks on a shift, and the name of the car ahead rolls over when it changes. The halo also gets a second layout that sits on the car's own halo in the default camera. Two more HUD parts join in the broadcast look, the pit lane timer and the lap time card, and every part of Project Halo can now be switched off on its own.

## New

- **Halo animations:** a bright streak runs out along both wings when Boost or Overtake comes on, and repeats once a second while it stays on. The gear number ticks on every shift, and the RPM line turns white near the limiter. When the car ahead changes, its name rolls out and the new one rolls in. The active aero bars turn between their two shapes instead of jumping. The Animations setting switches all of it off.
- **Halo layout: Default camera.** A new, even-sided halo, larger, placed on the car's own halo as the default T-cam shows it, with bigger gear numbers. It is the new default. The setting Halo layout gives the earlier halo back as TV offset (the broadcast's off-centre camera angle, at the bottom of the screen).
- **Pit lane timer:** in place of the game's pit timer, in the broadcast look: position, team logo, surname, team colour line, IN PIT with the pit lane time, and the stop time under it. After the pit exit the time shows with three decimals.
- **Lap time card:** in place of the game's lap time pills: position, team logo, surname and tyre, the running lap time, and S1, S2 and S3. The bar of the current sector grows in white and takes the game's sector colour when the sector is done. The lap time turns green for 3 seconds on a personal best and purple on the session's fastest lap. Best and Previous sit below.
- **Pit speed message:** the whole message is red while you are over the pit limit and green once you are under it, with PIT LIMIT above the limit.
- **A switch for every part:** Halo dial, Timing tower, Race Control banner, Pit lane timer, Lap time card and Pit speed colour each have their own setting. Off gives that part of the game's own HUD back. The Timing tower switches at once; the others apply after a restart. Pit speed colour needs the Race Control banner on.

## Changed

- The pit lane timer and the lap time card take their team logo and tyre from the same source as the tower, and work with the Timing tower switched off.

## Fixed

- View highlights (after a race): the timing tower now shows in the highlights reel, with each clip's order, team logos, tyres and lap. It shows no gaps there, because the game does not keep them for a replayed moment.
- Replays: an instant replay no longer risks showing the game's board behind the tower.

## Known issues

- Halo layout Default camera: fitted to a 2026 car in the default T-cam at 16:9. Other cars, other cameras, ultrawide screens and changed camera settings can sit differently: move or resize the halo in HUD customisation, or use TV offset.
- Halo layout Default camera: a halo you already moved in HUD customisation ends up higher and larger. Place it again once.
- Halo layout Default camera: the game's tutorial message and the open MFD can touch the halo.
- The pit window stays the game's own.
- The running lap time shows three decimals; the game gives the HUD no shorter form.
- STOP TIME and PIT LIMIT are in English in every language.
- My Team: your own team's logo stays empty in the tower.
- Time Trial: long driver names in the tower look squeezed.
- Full field with more than 22 cars: the tower can run past the bottom of the screen. Make it smaller in HUD customisation, or use Around me or Leaders.
- With the timing tower on and Track Position switched off in HUD customisation, the game's lap counter stays hidden too. Turn the Timing tower setting off to get it back.
- Depending on the screen resolution, the scaling might be off.

## Setup

Steam version of F1 25 with the official 2026 Season Pack, and Swofty Launcher 1.8.36 or newer. Install or update Project Halo from the Addon Browser in the launcher, or import the zip there, then start the game.

Full notes: https://github.com/nyannoying1337/f1-25-project-halo/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

# Project Halo 0.2.1 beta

The validation log now stays inside the game folder. Nothing changes in the halo or the timing tower. Everything from 0.2.0 is in this release.

## Changed

- **Validation log:** the two CSV files are now written to swofty\addons\nick.f1-2026-halo\diag in the F1 25 game folder, through the Swofty launcher's own storage. They used to go to a folder under %LOCALAPPDATA%. The launcher keeps the files between sessions. The option is still off by default.

Full notes: https://github.com/nyannoying1337/f1-25-project-halo/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

# Project Halo 0.2.0 beta

The timing tower now moves like the broadcast: when cars change places, their rows slide into their new positions, and flag cards slide in and out of the header. The tower also shows lap times in practice and qualifying and the fastest lap in races, follows the Spectator Menu and takes fields of up to 30 cars. The halo looks closer to the broadcast.

## New

- **Tower animations:** when cars change places, their rows slide into their new positions, fast at first and then settling, like the broadcast. The position arrow rides in with its row, and the position number and a new best lap time fade in. Flag cards (yellow flag, VSC, safety car, red flag, chequered flag) slide down out of the header and the rows move down with them; when the flag ends, the card rolls back up and the rows close the gap. The new Animations setting (On) switches them off: then every change shows at once, as before.
- **Lap times in practice and qualifying:** the tower shows the leader's best lap and every other car's gap to it. A new personal best flashes green for 2 seconds, a new session best purple. The header shows the session's clock.
- **Knockout zone:** in Q1 and Q2 (SQ1 and SQ2 in sprint qualifying), a red hatch marks the cars in the knockout zone.
- **Fastest lap in races:** a purple stopwatch beside the car with the fastest lap.
- **Spectator view:** the tower follows the Spectator Menu's Gap (None, Interval, Leader, Fastest Lap) and Detail (None, Position Change, Stops, Tyre, Best, Penalties) options. Fastest Lap shows thousandths in practice and qualifying, tenths in races.
- **Up to 30 cars:** Full field shows every car on bigger grids, such as the 24 cars of a My Team career.

## Changed

- **Halo look:** closer to the broadcast in every copy (2026, 2025 and F2 cars, the HUD editor and the spectator view): the collar fades out towards the top, and the face is see-through with a fine grid. The TURN label shows only with a turn number, and BRAKE stands upright.
- **Timing tower:** the position arrows show for 3 seconds (was 4), and P1's red box steps aside while an arrow shows. The virtual safety car card is taller and easier to read.
- **Icon:** the addon icon shows the whole dial.

## Fixed

- Practice and qualifying: no empty lap counter box or flag box above the tower any more.
- Spectator view: the tower's top five rows look like the rest, and its header shows the FIA logo once.
- Spectator view: the game's own flag message (LAP, CAUTION, SECTOR) no longer draws over the tower's yellow flag card; it hides while the tower shows.
- Qualifying: at the end of a session, cars with a lap time keep their row and time instead of showing Out for a few seconds.

## Known issues

- My Team: your own team's logo stays empty in the tower.
- Time Trial: long driver names in the tower look squeezed.
- Full field with more than 22 cars: the tower can run past the bottom of the screen. Make it smaller in HUD customisation, or use Around me or Leaders.
- With the timing tower on and Track Position switched off in HUD customisation, the game's lap counter stays hidden too. Turn the Timing tower setting off to get it back.
- Depending on the screen resolution, the scaling might be off.

## Setup

Steam version of F1 25 with the official 2026 Season Pack, and Swofty Launcher 1.8.36 or newer. Install or update Project Halo from the Addon Browser in the launcher, or import the zip there, then start the game.

Full notes: https://github.com/nyannoying1337/f1-25-project-halo/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

# Project Halo 0.1.2 beta

A broadcast-style timing tower joins the halo, and the halo now also works in F1 25's 2025 and F2 cars and in the spectator view.

## New

- **Timing tower:** in place of the Track Position list, from the game's own classification. Positions, team logos and colours, driver codes, intervals or gaps to the leader, tyres, PIT, Out, DSQ and NC, and a green or red arrow when a car gains or loses a place. Its header shows the lap or the session, and the safety car, virtual safety car, yellow flag, red flag and chequered flag. Practice, qualifying, races, Time Trial, replays and the spectator view. Move, resize or hide it in HUD customisation.
- **Race Control banner:** the game's own race messages, in the style of the broadcast's Race Control banner.
- **2025 and F2 cars:** the halo replaces their dials too. 2025 cars show DRS, the ERS deploy mode, the battery and Recharge and Deploy. F2 cars show DRS, without the energy parts. The setting Halo in 2025 and F2 cars gives them their own dials back.
- **Spectator view:** the halo shows the car you watch, and the tower replaces the spectator board with that car highlighted.
- **G-force meter:** optional, off by default. The 2026 broadcast's G-force meter in the middle of the halo.

## Fixed

- Four turn arrows pointed the wrong way: Sakhir T5, Silverstone T10 and Mexico City T15 now point left, Baku T9 right.
- The turn number moved on to the next turn about 35 m early at some circuits. After a lap the halo now lines its turn list up with the track.
- The spectator HUD's dial no longer shows every part of the halo at once.

## Known issues

- Spectator view: the tower does not follow the Spectator Menu's Gap (None, Leader, Fastest Lap) and Detail (Position Change, Stops, Tyre, Penalties) options yet. It keeps its own Gap mode.
- Spectator view: the tower's top five rows look a little different from the rest, and its header shows the FIA logo twice.
- Depending on the screen resolution, the scaling might be off.
- Practice and qualifying: the tower shows no lap times yet.

Full notes: https://github.com/nyannoying1337/f1-25-project-halo/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

# Project Halo 0.1.1 beta

The addon's Swofty manifest now says that it supports the Steam version of F1 25 only and needs Swofty Launcher 1.8.36 or newer. Nothing changes in the game. Everything from 0.1.0 is in this release.

Full notes: https://github.com/nyannoying1337/f1-25-project-halo/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

# Project Halo 0.1.0 beta

First public release: the onboard halo graphic from the 2026 F1 world feed, in place of the 2026 dial of F1 25's 2026 Season Pack.

## New

- **The 2026 halo:** speed in km/h and mph, gear and revs, throttle and brake, the battery, Recharge and Deploy, Boost, Overtake and Active Aero, your position and the car ahead, and the next turn.
- **Drawn by the game:** move and resize it in HUD customisation like any other element. It hides when the game hides its HUD.
- **No telemetry:** the halo reads the running game itself and changes nothing in it. No UDP telemetry, no companion app.
- **Settings:** driver names and turn numbers can be switched off. A validation log, off by default, records what the halo reads.

## Known issues

- Recharge, Deploy, Boost and Active Aero are not confirmed in the game yet. Driven so far: practice at Bahrain.
- When you spectate, the 2026 dial in the spectator HUD can show every part of the halo at once, with no live values.

Full notes: https://github.com/nyannoying1337/f1-25-project-halo/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

addons.name: F2 Revamp
addons.author: miguelvf3
addons.summary: A Driver Career that starts in the 2026 Formula 2 season: finish well to earn an F1 seat, while the best F2 drivers move up too. Its own tile and save slots; the stock 2026 career is unchanged.
addons.description:
F2 Revamp adds a new Driver Career for F1 25 (2026 season) that starts in Formula 2. Race the real 2026 F2 grid and calendar, then move up to Formula 1 for 2027. It has its own tile in the career menu and its own save slots, so the game's own career is unchanged.

## **Features**

- **The 2026 F2 season:** the real grid (Câmara, Herta, Tsolov, Mini...) and calendar, Melbourne first, with Madrid. 14, 8 or 3 rounds.
- **Earn your seat:** F1 teams follow your whole F2 season: points, wins, poles and how you do against your teammate. Each team has its own bar to fill. Teams outside your academy are harder to convince, and Mercedes, Ferrari, Red Bull and McLaren hardest of all. A refused team tells you why and which teams are open.
- **Super licence:** you need 40 points for a seat. Your F2 place gives most of them, and the real F2 drivers bring points from their earlier seasons.
- **Career panel:** press F8 (or open the F2 Revamp tab at Team HQ) to see the F2 table, your season, your super licence and every F1 team's interest in you.
- **Academy targets:** your academy sets a target for each F2 round, harder as you score more. Meeting them helps with its teams. Miss three in a row and it drops you.
- **Academies matter:** Ferrari juniors find it easiest to join Haas, Mercedes juniors Aston Martin and Red Bull juniors Racing Bulls. Alpine, Williams, Audi and Cadillac juniors join their own team. McLaren juniors and drivers with no academy go to Cadillac or Aston Martin. Real F2 drivers keep their real academies.
- **F2 drivers move up too:** at your first F1 Team HQ the best AI drivers of your F2 season replace Ocon at Haas and Lawson and Lindblad at Racing Bulls. A message reviews your F2 season and names them, and the panel shows the rookie standings in your first F1 season.
- **The 2027 F1 calendar:** 22 rounds, with GP and championship titles reading 2027. Shorter 16 and 10-round seasons too.
- **Optional rounds:** Portugal (Portimão) and Turkey (Istanbul Park), each with its own setting. They need their track addons.
- **Works with Silly Season:** it waits for your F2 season to end and takes the promotions as signings.
- **Skip to F1** is still there and goes straight to F1 with every team open.

## Requirements

- Swofty Launcher 1.9.34 or later with Swofty Core 0.2.13 or later, and F1 25 with the 2026 season.
- Made and tested on the Steam copy of the game. The EA app copy is allowed, but I haven't tested it.
- Optional: Portimão by Pajko and Istanbul Park by Apoc & RK, for the two extra rounds. Each setting unlocks when its track addon is on. Turn both on before starting a career.

## How to play

1. Turn F2 Revamp on in your profile.
2. Driver Career > Addons row > **F2 2026 > F1 2027**.
3. Pick a driver and choose **Start in F2**.
4. Press F8 at any time to open the career panel.

## Known issues

- The Custom Season screen's long season button reads "24 Races"; the list under it has this career's 22 to 24 rounds.
- In F2 the career panel only opens with F8.
- On a tie on points, the place in the refusal popup can be one off the game's standings.
- A promoted driver can be missing from the Driver Rating Comparison.
- You can't repeat F2 after a poor season yet.
- With two saved careers of the same driver, Continue from the main menu uses the data of the one played last. Pick the save from the load list to be sure.

Found a problem? Send your logs through Swofty and say what you were doing.

## Credits

Career layout and 2026 titles from Swofty's Progressive Career (AGPL-3.0-or-later). Portimão by Pajko and Istanbul Park by Apoc & RK are separate addons. Source: https://github.com/miguelvf3/miguel-s-f1-25-mods

addons.author: Dejw
addons.summary: Historical calendars for Swofty Progressive Career, 2013-2026. Steam: tested. EA app: compatibility pending confirmation; launcher-resolved bindings are used, but EA has not been tested. Choose optional historical circuits in Grand Prix settings. addons.description:
**Race the calendar that matches your year in Swofty’s Progressive Career.**

Historical Calendar brings season-specific schedules to F1 25 Driver Career from **2016 through 2026**. Version **1.0.0**

### How to use it in game

1. Start a new **Progressive Career** and select your **Starting Season**.
2. On the season length screen, choose **Full Season** to load that year’s calendar.
3. At the end of the season, select **Historical Calendar** on the calendar selection screen and confirm to load the next year’s schedule.

### Optional tracks

**Sepang, Hockenheim, Sochi, Paul Ricard, Portimão, Jerez, Nürburgring, Istanbul Park and Bahrain Outer** each have their own toggle. All nine are off by default. The calendar uses standard F1 25 circuits in those slots, keeping the number and order of rounds.

To use an optional circuit, install and enable its track add-on separately in the same launcher profile, turn on its toggle in **Historical Calendar**, and rebuild or restart through the launcher. If the track add-on is missing or disabled, the launcher shows a warning and uses the substitute. For example, **Losail fills the Sepang round in 2016 and 2017** when Sepang is off.

Track settings apply when a calendar is created. Weekend formats, including sprints, follow the game or the installed track add-on.

**Credits**  
Calendar mod by **Dejw**. Thanks to **Swofty** for Progressive Career and the launcher SDK, and to the creators of the optional track add-ons.

addons.name: Driver Momentum
addons.author: Alex Sánchez
addons.summary: AI drivers have a weekend form that follows their season: hot streaks and slumps from their results in Driver Career and My Team, veterans steadier than rookies, and a thermal Form Guide (F6). Based on msyeett's Driver Form.
addons.description:
AI drivers have a weekend form, and in **Driver Career** and **My Team** that form follows their season: hot streaks, slumps, steady veterans and rookies who swing. Press **F6** in a session for the **Form Guide**. Built on **msyeett's Driver Form**, with everything it does.

### Weekend form
- Every AI driver is in form, out of form or neutral for the weekend. It lasts through practice, qualifying and the race, even if you close the game between sessions.
- In form: quicker over a lap through the game's own AI pace, hot spells of extra time, harder to pass.
- Out of form: slower, they brake earlier, carry less speed and get on the throttle later, with bad patches and sudden mistakes.
- Your own car is never touched. Time Trial is left alone.

### Momentum
- After every race a driver's streak moves with their result: better than their usual finish and further ahead of their teammate than usual, it goes up; worse, it goes down. A slow car or a faster teammate is no slump by itself.
- A retirement leaves the streak as it is, a sprint counts half, and a streak fades without results to back it.
- Veterans' form swings less than rookies', from the game's experience and awareness ratings.
- Each career remembers its streaks and every driver's last five results.

### Form Guide
- A drawer that reads the grid like a thermal camera: every driver's heat index from -100 to +100 on a thermometer, the time a lap it is worth, the grid's heat as an equaliser, and the hottest and coldest driver.
- In a career, each driver's trend over their last five races as a line, and those results as cells coloured by how hot they were.
- HOT STREAK, SLUMP, FLYING, STRUGGLING, STEADY and ERRATIC tags, and live ON A CHARGE, LOSING TIME and MISTAKE marks during the race.
- It doesn't take the keys from the game: drive with it open. Three sizes.

### Settings
Find these in **ADDON SETTINGS**.
- **Form strength**: Off, Subtle (about 0.8 s a lap either way), Normal (1.5 s), Wild (2.2 s) or Chaos (3.5 s).
- **Momentum**: how much the streak counts in a career. Off is a fresh roll every weekend, like Driver Form.
- **Form Guide key**: F6, F5, F9, F10, F11 or None. **Form Guide size**: Small, Normal or Large.
- **In form / Out of form toasts**, **Bad patches and mistakes**, and how often the race **Messages** show. Everything on screen except the Form Guide and its reminder is off by default.

### Works with
- Silly Season and other career addons. Drivers added by other addons get a form too.
- Not with Driver Form itself: turn one of the two off.
- Team Orders and other addons that change the AI work, and their effects add up.

### Needs
Swofty Launcher 1.8.36 or later. Steam.

### Credits
- Driver Form: msyeett (MIT)
- Driver Momentum: Alex Sánchez
- Swofty Launcher: Swofty

Unofficial fan addon, not affiliated with or endorsed by EA, Codemasters or Formula 1.

addons.name: Silly Season
addons.author: Alex Sánchez
addons.summary: A living driver market for Career mode: rumours, talks, signings, retirements, sackings, press conferences, F2 and new talents, with inbox mails, breaking news and a market panel (F7).
addons.description:
# Silly Season — a living driver market for F1 25

F1 25's career barely has a driver market. Silly Season gives it one. Through the season the paddock talks: rumours appear, some turn into talks and official signings, others fall apart. Veterans retire, impatient teams sack drivers in the middle of the year and the academies push their F2 youngsters. When the new season starts, the game's grid really changes.

## How you follow it
- **Inbox mails** from a paddock insider: a market preview before every race weekend, a radar after the race and the new grid when the season closes.
- **Breaking-news banner:** a broadcast-style lower third for every official signing, retirement or sacking.
- **The market hub (F7, or Back + Y on a pad):** a full-screen panel with a live headline ticker and 13 pages:
  - Paddock, News, Press, Rumours, Deals, next season's Grid;
  - a Drivers ranking, Contracts, a driver Stock chart;
  - Formula 2, Engineers, Free agents and History.
- **Team HQ tab:** reports, the main settings and a count of unread news.

## What happens in the market
- **Rumours from fictional outlets with a reliability rating.** The reliable ones are usually right, the tabloids not so much.
- **Teams choose like real teams.** They look at car level, prestige, form, age and potential. They favour their own academy drivers, and a big team can buy out a star's contract.
- **Retirements and sackings:**
  - veterans retire from 34;
  - in the middle of the season a team can sack a driver who is on a bad run;
  - a driver clearly beaten by his team-mate comes under pressure.
- **Press conferences.** Journalists ask about your future, your team-mate and other drivers. Your answers shape rumours, renewals and rivalries.
- **New talents** with their own names join F2 every season. F2 is simulated, and its podium gets noticed by F1 teams.
- **More depth:**
  - stand-ins for injured drivers;
  - technical directors who change teams and move the car's level;
  - drivers who bring sponsors;
  - exit clauses tied to the constructors' championship;
  - garage feuds;
  - estimated salaries;
  - an end-of-season review.
- **Your own seat is never touched.** You can also protect your team-mate.

## Settings
- Intensity: realistic, lively or chaos.
- How many rumours appear.
- Mid-season changes.
- Legends on the market.
- Pop-ups, mails, banner and hub.
- Who runs the market: Silly Season or the game.

Change them in ADDON SETTINGS or in the Team HQ tab.

## Requirements
- Swofty Launcher 1.8.16 or later.
- Driver Career and My Team, 2025 and 2026 seasons.
- The banner and the hub use Swofty's experimental overlay. Mails and the Team HQ tab work without it.

## Good to know
- The market state lives with your career. Loading an older save doesn't roll the market back.
- With frame generation on (DLSS FG or FSR), the overlay may not draw.

Silly Season keeps working after a game update, even before the launcher catches up. This update introduces **On-Track Reputation (experimental)**, allowing overtakes, incidents and mechanical failures to influence driver form, market value and team interest through UDP telemetry.

**Driver transfers are now safer**, preserving line-ups from other addons and verifying every seat change against the game's actual grid. **Progressive Career** now correctly recognises historical seasons from 2014 onwards, while **F2 Revamp 0.8.1 and 0.9.0** are fully supported.

Race tracking has been improved to prevent duplicated results, missing races and unexpected market resets. Career saves are also more reliable, with **over 60% smaller files and approximately 40% faster processing**.

The market panel can now open during paused sessions, supports custom keys (F6–F11) and features a cleaner interface with improved overlays and race reports. Numerous additional fixes improve stability, My Team compatibility and driver identification.

On-track reputation
- New option, on by default; needs UDP Telemetry on in the game's settings.
- Silly Season now reads your races' overtakes, collisions and retirements from the game's telemetry:
  - Overtakes lift a driver's form and value, and past half distance the season's best overtaker makes the news ("OVERTAKE KING").
  - Incidents cost form; the third and fifth of a season make a story, and teams fighting at the front shy away from incident-prone drivers.
  - A mechanical failure no longer counts against the driver's form. The team takes the blame, and its third breakdown of the season makes a reliability story.
  - Driver cards show the season's overtakes, incidents and mechanical DNFs. Without UDP telemetry the market runs on results alone, as before.
The F7 panel opens while a session is paused
- The F7 panel opens while a session is paused, to check the market mid-weekend.
- It closes when you go back to the session; the other overlays still wait for Team HQ.
Log improvements
- The log now says whether you own the F1 2026 season content, to help with reports.

- Installs on every launcher that can run it.
- 1.1.0 asked for launcher 1.8.16 or later, but its manifest links the source code, which launchers before 1.8.19 refuse.
- Silly Season now asks for launcher 1.8.36 or later.
- Tagged "Steam" in the Addon Browser:
- The copy of the game it was tested on, instead of "Not tested".
- F7 panel and banner:
- The README no longer says they need SWOFTY_OVERLAY_FG=1 with Frame Generation (the launcher draws them since 1.8.25).
- If they never show on an NVIDIA card with DLSS, update the launcher to 1.8.38.

1. History mode and Progressive Career
- History mode for Progressive Career on the Swofty Seasons. Silly Season now plays along with Progressive's real seasons (2015 to 2026): it tells next year's real moves through the season as rumours, talks and official signings, announces the real retirements and the real mid-season stand-ins at the right race, and closes each season with the real grid. It never touches a seat while the real years last: Progressive puts each line-up on the grid. Each year's team names, car pace and driver ratings come from Progressive's data, and the drivers of the season addons (Vettel, Räikkönen, Kubica, Schumacher...) are part of the market. From 2026 on, Silly Season's own market takes over.
- Progressive Career's 2015 to 2018 seasons: the drivers of those years (Rosberg, Massa, Maldonado, Vandoorne...) have their real names and ages, and Rosberg retires as champion.
- F2 Revamp support (miguelvf3's career that starts in F2 2026):
  - Silly Season stays out of the way while you race F2.
  - It starts the market with your first F1 season (2027) and treats the drivers F2 Revamp promotes as signings with their two-year contracts.
  - The two addons talk through Swofty services: Silly Season now publishes silly_season.market for other addons.
- Konnersport joins the market in 2025 careers that have the eleventh team: its seats are planned, Aiden Jackson and Callie Mayer can move, and other drivers can sign for it. In careers without it, nothing changes.
2. The real season and race results
- The real season. Race results come from your career's standings, round by round: form, points, pressure, sackings, the driver stock and the constructors' order (next year's cars, exit clauses) follow what really happens on track, and the standings count the rounds raced. If they can't be read, races are simulated as before.
- Season awards from your career's results: champion, constructors, rookie of the year, beat the car and most improved, in the news and in a Hall of Fame on the History page.
- Standings (F7): a new page with the drivers' and constructors' championships from the real results, My Team included. Click a line for the driver's or the team's card.
- Career totals: each driver's starts, wins, podiums, titles and teams across the seasons of your career, on his card, and a Records section on the History page.
- Farewells: a driver who retires says goodbye at the season's last race with his career in numbers, and the season review pays tribute.
3. Driver personalities and team plans
- Drivers have a character. Each one is ambitious, loyal or after the money, to a degree. Loyal drivers renew more often and for longer, and are hard to buy out. Ambitious stars turn down seats below their level, sign with exit clauses and can ask to leave a slow car despite their contract. Money-minded drivers cost more and follow the budget. You see it in the news and on the Drivers page.
- Teams have a plan: title push, contender, rebuild, youth or survival, from their car, brand, budget and results. A title team signs proven drivers and has no patience; a rebuilding team bets on youth; a team fighting to survive loves a driver with sponsors. The plan can change at mid-season, and the season preview and the Grid page show it.
- Team principals: every team has one (invented). A team far below where its car belongs can sack him, and the new principal brings his own plan.
- Team-mate duel on each driver's card: how many races he finished ahead of his current team-mate this season.
- Your Future (F7): a new page about you: your value race by race, your contract, how each team rates you (keen, watching or cool, with the seats that open), how your team feels about you, and everything the paddock says about you. In My Team, your team's place in the constructors' order against the teams either side of it.
4. The transfer market
- The domino effect. A signing waits until the seat it goes to is free, so moves fall in order. When a transfer goes official, the seat it leaves opens at once, and the team's next choice goes straight into talks ("DOMINO EFFECT: X NEXT FOR Y").
- Deadline day: the last two races before the grid is set. Deals close fast, there can be a last-minute swoop nobody saw coming, and the F7 header, the ticker and the banner count down.
- The odds of every story: each rumour and each link of the Transfer Centre shows its chance of ending in a signing, from what the paddock can see (the stage, who reports it, whether the driver wants the seat, deadline day).
- Sister-team swaps: Red Bull can swap a struggling driver with Racing Bulls' driver in form mid-season, as in real life.
- Money moves: sponsors join a team doing better than its car and leave one doing worse, and the constructors' order pays prize money each winter. The budget shapes the team's plan and salaries, and the team card shows how it moved this season.
- New talents get their own racing number once they reach F1.
- Secret meetings: when the game puts a secret meeting with another team on your calendar, the paddock hears of it.
- New press topics with consequences: deadline day ("does your team need a signing?"), a rival's bombshell signing, your own renewal and last season's awards. Asking for reinforcements makes your team hunt a proven driver, and what you say about your contract changes how comfortable your team is with you, which brings renewal talk or suitors.
- Scouting page (F7): a shortlist of the drivers available next season who fit your team, with how keen each one is. In My Team, your scout also sends a report twice a season for your second seat.
5. Driver and team information
- Driver cards (F7): click a driver, or pick him with Up/Down and press Enter/A, for his full card: value and potential, contract and salary, character, this season's points, wins and podiums, a race-by-race value chart (this season against the last), his career path, the stories about him and his honours.
- Team cards (F7): from the Grid and Engineers pages: the team's plan, car, prestige, budget and technical director, this season's and next season's line-ups, its academy and reserves, its market moves and honours.
- Transfer Centre (F7): a new page with every chain of moves, domino by domino, and the signings still waiting for their seat.
- Drivers from other addons join the market. Silly Season now reads your career's own driver lists from the game, so the free agents another addon adds (More Driver Models, for example) can be signed, show in Free agents and Scouting, and have their own cards. Icons of the past only come back with the Legends option.
- Drivers it didn't know get their real ratings and names. A driver of another season put on the grid with an editor (Team & Driver Editor, Career Mode Editor) now gets his ratings and his name from the game, instead of a default 70.
- My Team's own team is the twelfth team in the F7 hub: it shows on the Grid, Drivers and Contracts pages with you and your team-mate, has its own card, takes its place in the constructors' order and can win the constructors' award. The market still never touches its seats.
6. Academies and reserves
- Academies and reserves:
- Every team has a reserve driver, starting with the game's own. Each winter, once the grid is final, the teams keep or sign theirs for next season (one news item lists them all). Racing Bulls shares Red Bull's, and Haas shares Ferrari's.
- Once a season the academies sign young drivers from F2 and the free agents, and an academy driver gets a better shot at his team's seats.
- Rookies come in through the second or partner team first (Racing Bulls before Red Bull, Haas before Ferrari).
- For a stand-in, the team calls the better of its reserve and its academy drivers on the day.
- Free agents show their role (reserve or academy, and whose) on the Free agents page and on their card; the team card names its reserve.
- The reserves live in Silly Season's market: Swofty can set the race seats, not the game's own reserve slot.
- New option, Academies and reserves, to turn it all off.
7. My Team and career progression
- Mid-season sackings really happen in the game. In 1.0.1 a sacking could be announced ("X out, Y takes the seat from the next race") while the game kept the old driver: the game only seats race drivers and free agents, and the replacement was often a reserve or an F2 driver. Silly Season now reads who the game will seat and only brings in those drivers, mid-season and for stand-ins. If the game still turns a change down, the market takes it back before you see it: no news, no move, the driver keeps his seat. A driver sacked by 1.0.1 whom the game kept racing is no longer treated as a free agent.
- Stand-ins: a reserve the game wouldn't seat is asked for by his id; if the game still refuses, the stand-in and its news are called off.
- A signing the game refuses at the new season is taken back. The market reads the game's grid again. If you hadn't seen the signing yet, it disappears; if you had, a "DEAL OFF" story says the move fell through. A driver whose successor the game refused races on instead of being retired.
- Next season's grid only uses drivers the game can seat (race drivers and free agents, not reserves), as mid-season sackings already did.
- Drivers from other addons join the market. Silly Season now reads your career's own driver lists from the game, so the free agents another addon adds (More Driver Models, for example) can be signed, show in Free agents and Scouting, and have their own cards. Icons of the past only come back with the Legends option.
8. Media, news and press
- The media keep score. Every outlet's reliability now moves with the stories it gets right or wrong, and newsrooms change a little each winter. At the season's close, a media scorecard names who got it right.
- Bombshell signing cards: a star's big move gets a full card with both teams' colours instead of the usual banner.
- Stacked news: the updates of one story (rumour, talks, official) stack into one card on the News page, and when several stories arrive at once the banner shows how many are waiting and moves faster.
- The headline ticker shows only the first line of lists (the grid, the awards) instead of drawing them over each other.
- Richer mails: the radar mail now covers deadline day and the seats still open, the chains of moves and the year's most reliable outlet; the grid mail adds the awards and the farewells.
- New press topics with consequences: deadline day ("does your team need a signing?"), a rival's bombshell signing, your own renewal and last season's awards. Asking for reinforcements makes your team hunt a proven driver, and what you say about your contract changes how comfortable your team is with you, which brings renewal talk or suitors.
9. New and redesigned overlays
- New and redesigned overlays:
  - One overlay at a time, the most important first, and never during a session or while the F7 panel is open. Full-screen moments can be skipped with Esc or A.
  - Breaking-news banner: the driver's initials in his team's colour, the team's livery behind the story and an icon for each kind of news.
  - Bombshell signing: both teams crash together, gold sparks fly, the driver's value counts up and the new team's boss has his say.
  - Grid reveal: where each new driver comes from, who leaves each team and a summary at the end.
  - Team HQ card: the last three headlines, the deadline countdown as a ring and your place in the championship.
  - Press questions on screen: at Team HQ the question shows with its three answers; press 1, 2 or 3 to answer, or F7 to read it in the panel.
  - Report after each race: back at Team HQ, a card with your value, new rumours, done deals and the teams following you.
  - Interest alerts: a small alert when a team becomes keen on you.
  - Awards ceremony: when the season closes, the awards are handed out one by one on a full screen.
  - Season cover: the first Team HQ visit of each season opens with the year, every team's plan and the winter's moves.
  - Farewell card for each driver who retires, and a red strip when deadline day opens.
  - New options to turn off the press questions on screen, the race report, the awards ceremony and the season cover.
- The grid reveal: once next season's grid is final, your next Team HQ visit reveals it team by team on a full screen. Press R on the Grid page to see it again.
- Team HQ card: a small card in a corner of Team HQ for a few seconds, with unread news, the latest headline and the deadline countdown.
- The breaking-news banner draws in full in the game (it could show only its white strip).
10. F7 panel and navigation
- A better F7 panel:
  - Season bar in the header: the round you're at, the mid-season window and deadline day, and the grid's close.
  - Ratings radar on every driver's card (pace, racecraft, awareness, experience, with the peak he can reach).
  - Standings show each driver's last five races in colour and his gap to the leader.
  - Rumours show each story's chance as a ring, and can be searched, sorted (by chance too) and filtered by team.
  - Paddock: the team keenest on you, and the top three of the championship.
  - Pages slide in from their side. The menu shows how many teams are keen on you and your place in the championship.
  - Everything opens its card: news, deals, moves, the stock, F2 (the podium too), the drivers on the Grid page.
  - Step through cards: a card opened from a list goes to the previous or next one with Left/Right (LB/RB), and shows "3 / 20".
  - Find anyone: / (Y on a pad) on any page without a table searches every driver and team.
  - The right stick scrolls, the scroll bar can be dragged with the mouse, and every page remembers where you left it.
  - Press: your answer stays on screen as "Answer sent" until the paddock reacts.
  - New option, Panel size (F7): small, normal or large.
  - The tables are sorted and filtered once when something changes, not every frame.
- Search, sort and filter on the Drivers, Contracts, Free agents and Scouting pages: type with / to search, S (X on a controller) to sort, F (Y) to filter by team or character.
- The side menu of the F7 panel fits its 17 pages on any screen.
- The race count no longer falls behind when the game reports every session as practice.
11. Options
- New options to turn each block off: Driver personalities, Team plans, Deadline day, Bombshell signing cards, Grid reveal, Team HQ market card and Racing numbers for new talents.
- New option, Living paddock: turn off the sister-team swaps, the moving budgets and the team principals.
- New option, Academies and reserves, to turn it all off.
- New option, Panel size (F7): small, normal or large.
- New options to turn off the press questions on screen, the race report, the awards ceremony and the season cover.
12. Fixes and improvements
- Fixes in 1.1.0's own blocks:
  - The team-mate duel counted wrong when several races were read at once.
  - Simulated races were filed a round late.
  - A reserve called up in a sacking the game refused lost his reserve role.
  - In-season moves showed the next year on the career path.
  - A press question claimed your contract ends this year, which the game doesn't tell.
- Fixes from 1.0.1 reports:
  - My Team: the news no longer announces signings that never happen. In My Team, Swofty can't change the race seats, so in 1.0.1 the winter's signings were announced but the grid stayed as the game had it. Silly Season now follows the market there: rumours, talks, odds and the press go on as before, but it never signs, sacks or retires anyone itself. It reports each move as official once the driver turns up in his new car, and the stories that predicted it come true. One news item explains this the first time.
  - A signing the game refuses at the new season is taken back. The market reads the game's grid again. If you hadn't seen the signing yet, it disappears; if you had, a "DEAL OFF" story says the move fell through. A driver whose successor the game refused races on instead of being retired.
  - Next season's grid only uses drivers the game can seat (race drivers and free agents, not reserves), as mid-season sackings already did.
  - The hub shows the game's own ratings. Silly Season now reads each driver's ratings from your career at every Team HQ: the overall rating the game shows (perks, specialists and the car included) and all five statistics, focus too. The market decides on them, so values, interest and who signs whom follow what the game shows instead of drifting from it over the seasons. Driver cards and Your Future show the game's Rating next to Silly Season's Market value (the rating plus current form), and the ratings radar has five axes. If the ratings can't be read, the market keeps its own numbers and says so in the log.
  - A driver's results are no longer lost when the game races him as a story team's copy (Konnersport's drivers in 2025 careers).
  - Driver progression no longer overwrites the game's ratings. After a few seasons it could swing a driver by 20 to 30 points, because the game develops its drivers on its own and Swofty can't tell Silly Season where it took them. The option now moves the market's own view of each driver, and only the new talents' ratings reach the game.

Fixes, and the market now follows your save.
The real grid from your save. At every Team HQ, Silly Season reads who sits in each seat of your career. Transfers made with the Career Mode Editor, other addons' line-ups and a season already under way all reach the market, and drivers it didn't know join it with their game names.
Careers already in a later season (2030 in a 2026 career) get the right year: the market follows the game's season, contracts move on with it and veterans no longer on the grid have retired. A market saved in the wrong year by 1.0.0 is mended at the next Team HQ.
Your driver is always found, a created driver and 2026 careers included (no more "Who are you?").
My Team: your own team shows in the F7 hub, and your team-mate is protected: no other team signs him.
Teams Silly Season doesn't know (Konnersport, another addon's): their drivers stay where they are and aren't listed as free agents.
Your market survives Swofty's new career ids. Swofty now names careers by their save slot; a career started with 1.0.0 finds the market it saved under its old id.
A new career keeps its market. The game gives a new career a temporary id until its first save. The market now follows the change, and a career you left before that save finds its market again at the next load.
Careers don't mix. Two careers with the same driver could share a saved market. If the saved market is ahead of the career you load, a fresh one starts.
Race count. A weekend counts once its race is run. Practice or qualifying alone no longer moves the market a race forward.
New talents' ratings reach the game once a talent gets an F1 seat, instead of being refused while he is a reserve.
Launcher warning: a career that uses Silly Season is marked as needing it, so the launcher warns before Play if the addon is off.
Headlines that say who and where: "OCON TO ALPINE?", "SAINZ-MERCEDES TALKS COOL OFF", "STROLL UNDER PRESSURE", "THE PRESS ASK ABOUT YOUR FUTURE"... instead of the same "MARKET RUMOUR" over and over, in the hub, the ticker, the banner and the reports.
New option, Panel effects (F7): turn off the shadows, glows and animations for a lighter panel on slower PCs.
Lighter panel: text sizes are measured once and remembered instead of every frame.
The Team HQ tab's unread count updates as soon as you close the F7 panel.
Who runs the market explains that "The game" lets the game's own retirements and sackings clash with Silly Season's plans.
A career that meets Silly Season mid-season no longer counts the first race's points twice once race results can be read.
More detail in the log: each session's type, and when a weekend counts as raced.

First release. A living driver market for F1 25's Driver Career and My Team (2025 and 2026 careers).
The market: rumours from reliable and less reliable outlets, talks, signings, renewals, retirements and mid-season sackings. Teams pick by car level, prestige, form, age, potential and their junior academies. Your own seat is never touched.
The market hub (F7 / Back + Y): a full-screen, broadcast-style panel with a live headline ticker, animated cards,
gauges and charts, and 13 pages: a Paddock overview, news cards, press conferences, rumours with outlet reliability, done deals, next season's grid in team colours, a driver ranking, contracts, a driver stock chart, F2, technical directors, free agents and history.
News without menus: weekly inbox mails (market preview, post-race radar, next year's grid) and a broadcast-style breaking-news banner.
Press conferences: questions about your future, your team-mate and other drivers' moves. Your answers shape rumours, renewals and rivalries.
New talents: young drivers with their own names join F2 every season. F2 is simulated, and its podium gets noticed by F1 teams.
More depth: stand-ins for injured drivers, technical directors who change teams, drivers with sponsors, exit clauses, garage feuds, salaries and a season review.
Team HQ tab: reports and the main settings, plus a count of unread news.
Settings: intensity (realistic, lively, chaos), number of rumours, legends on the market, and more in ADDON SETTINGS.
Requires Swofty Launcher 1.8.16 or later. The banner and the hub use Swofty's experimental overlay.

addons.name: Improved Car Setups
addons.author: msyeett
addons.summary: On the car setup screen, every changed row shows how far it moved, and the right stick puts a row back.
addons.description:
Makes the car setup screen easier to work with. Every row you change shows how far it moved, right next to the value, so you always know what you touched. One button puts a row back.

### How it works
- A changed row shows its change in the row's own units: `27 +2` on a wing, `-3.40 +0.10` on camber, `24.3psi +0.1` on a tyre.
- Rows you haven't changed show nothing. Set a value back and its number goes away.
- Picking a preset or loading a saved setup shows that setup's changes too.
- The row you're on also shows last session's value when it was different, like `24 -1 last 27`. Kept per track, even after a game restart.
- Only your own car. No game files are replaced, so it works next to other menu addons.

### Reset a row
- Press the **right stick** (keyboard **F9**, or your wheel's button for it) on a setup row and it goes back to its start value.
- It goes through the game's own slider, so the value always stays one the game allows.

### Parc fermé
- With **Improved Parc Ferme** (0.1.3 or newer) on, rows locked after qualifying say **Locked**, and the description box tells you that changing one means starting from the pit lane.
- Reset never touches a locked row.

### Settings
- **Compare to:** what the numbers compare against. **Session start** (default) is your setup when the session started; **Preset 1-5** compares against one of the game's five presets for that track. Reset goes back to the same.

### Known gaps
- On a race grid after qualifying the change numbers don't show: the game hands your car to the AI there.

### Needs
- Swofty Launcher 1.8.36 or newer.
- Any mode with a garage setup screen: Time Trial, Grand Prix, Driver Career, My Team.
- Offline sessions only, like all modded play.

### Credits
- Addon: msyeett
- Swofty Launcher: Swofty

Unofficial fan addon, not affiliated with or endorsed by EA, Codemasters or Formula 1. Found a bug or something that looks off? Let me know on the Discord.

latest.changelog: - Works with the F1 25 game update of 16 November 2026 (before, the setup rows showed no changes).

versions.changelog: - Works with the F1 25 game update of 16 November 2026 (before, the setup rows showed no changes).

- Reset a row: press the right stick (F9 on a keyboard) on a setup row and it goes back to its start value.
- New setting "Compare to": compare against your setup at the session start (default) or one of the five presets.
  Reset goes back to the same.
- The row you're on shows last session's value when it was different, like `24 -1 last 27`. Kept per track, across
  game restarts.
- With Improved Parc Ferme 0.1.3 or newer: rows locked after qualifying say "Locked", and the description box tells
  you that changing one means a pit lane start. Reset skips locked rows.
- Known gap: on a race grid after qualifying the change numbers don't show (the game hands your car to the AI there).

addons.name: Grand Prix Saves
addons.author: msyeett
addons.summary: Keeps up to 10 offline Grand Prix saves instead of one: a card for each save on the Grand Prix screen, plus Create New.
addons.description:
Keeps up to **10 offline Grand Prix saves** instead of one. Every save gets its own card on the Grand Prix screen, so you can keep a championship, a one-off weekend and anything else side by side and jump between them.

### Your saves
- One card per save, newest first, with the team you drive for and when you last played it.
- Scroll with Up and Down. The panel on the right shows the selected save's track, round and standings.
- **Accept** continues the save you're on.
- **F2** deletes the selected save, after the game's own confirm. The list updates straight away.

### Create New
- The **Create New** card under your saves starts a new Grand Prix in a save of its own.
- No more "this will overwrite your existing Grand Prix" warning: your other saves stay.
- Change your mind and back out before the race? Your saves are still there next time.
- Up to 10 saves. At 10 the Create New card goes; delete one to make room.

### Needs
- Swofty Launcher 1.8.10 or newer.
- Offline sessions only, like all modded play.

### Credits
- Addon: msyeett
- Swofty Launcher: Swofty

Unofficial fan addon, not affiliated with or endorsed by EA, Codemasters or Formula 1. Found a bug or something that looks off? Let me know on the Discord.

latest.changelog: - Works with the F1 25 game update of 16 November 2026 (before, the saves cards were gone and the stock screen was back).

versions.changelog: - Works with the F1 25 game update of 16 November 2026 (before, the saves cards were gone and the stock screen was back).
- Cheaper memory checks with Swofty Launcher 1.9.30 or newer (fewer small hitches).

- With no saves, Grand Prix now opens the saves screen with just the Create New card, instead of going straight to
  a new Grand Prix (for example after backing out of one, or deleting your last save).
- Fixed Create New sometimes doing nothing when pressed.
- Shows as tested on Steam in the launcher's Addon Browser, in the Utility category. Needs launcher 1.8.36 or newer.

- Saves from season boxes (like SWOFTY Seasons 2017) now show up. Before, only Create New was offered.
- Fixed a crash when deleting a save with F2.
- Deleting your last save now updates the screen straight away.

- First release.
- Up to 10 Grand Prix saves, one card each on the Grand Prix screen, with a Create New card under them.
- Create New starts a new Grand Prix in its own save, with no overwrite warning.
- F2 deletes the selected save; leaving a new Grand Prix before it starts keeps your saves.

addons.name: Starting Grid
addons.author: msyeett
addons.summary: Adds the online Starting Grid setting and Grid Editor to the offline Grand Prix: Realistic, Reversed, Random or your own Custom Grid when qualifying is off. Offline only.
addons.description:
Brings the online **Starting Grid** setting and the **Grid Editor** to the offline **Grand Prix**. Pick how the grid lines up when you race without qualifying, or set the whole order yourself, just like in an online lobby. Works with the 2025 and 2026 seasons.

### Starting Grid
Find it in **Grand Prix → Settings → Weekend Structure**, with **Qualifying Format** set to **Off**.

- **Realistic**: the cars start roughly in performance order, the game's usual grid.
- **Reversed**: the slowest cars start at the front.
- **Random**: a completely random grid, different every race.
- **Custom Grid**: the order you set in the Grid Editor.

### Grid Editor
- The online Grid Editor, now with every driver in your Grand Prix.
- Move any driver up or down, yourself included, or hit **Randomise Grid**.
- The arrows show how far each driver moved from the game's own order.
- Opening the Grid Editor switches Starting Grid to Custom Grid for you.

### Kept with your save
- Your Starting Grid choice and custom order stay with your Grand Prix save, even if you close the game.
- Continue the save and they're back. Start a new Grand Prix and it starts fresh on Realistic.
- Delete the save or finish it, and they go with it.

### Needs

addons.name: Smarter AI Strategies
addons.author: Jonno
addons.summary: Live AI pit strategy with adaptive tyre-wear learning, team coordination and career awareness.
addons.description:
# Smarter AI Strategies

**Every AI team gets a strategist on the pit wall.** Instead of following fixed pit windows, the AI re-plans its
pit stops live from what's happening in the race, so strategy actually decides positions.

---

## NEW
- Adaptive Tyre Intelligence learns measured AI wear and uses compatible career or baseline knowledge when available. Your car is excluded, and the game still executes pit stops using its allocated sets.

## What changes

- **Undercuts and covers:** a car stuck behind a rival pits early to jump it, and the rival decides whether to
  cover or stay out.
- **Overcuts:** staying out in clean air when a rival's stop drops it into traffic.
- **Traffic-aware stops:** teams check where a car would rejoin and wait rather than drop it into a train.
- **Safety Car and VSC calls:** some cars take the cheap stop, others stay out for track position. Calls a car
  can't make in time are dropped when racing resumes.
- **Weather timing:** stops follow the track's wetness and its trend.
- **Team-mates:** no needless double stacks, and split strategies when one car should cover and the other run
  long.
- **Varied starting tyres:** some AI cars start on the tyre the game planned for later, so the grid isn't all on
  one compound.
- **Team styles:** conservative, balanced, opportunistic, aggressive or high-variance pit walls, so teams don't
  all behave the same. They misjudge things now and then too.
- **Driver Career and My Team:** championship leaders protect results, challengers gamble, and rivalries build
  over a season (kept per save). Your My Team only becomes a target once it's a contender.

---

## What stays the game's

The game still runs every stop: the number of stops, the tyre sets (always the ones it chose for that car),
tyre rules, pit lane rules and penalties. Every car still uses two dry compounds. **Your car is never touched.**

---

## Settings

| Setting | Default |
|---|---|
| Enable Smarter AI Strategies | On |
| Strategy intelligence | Competitive |
| Grand Prix dynamic rivals | On |
| Career championship awareness | On |
| Career persistent rivalries | On |
| AI undercut / overcut intelligence | On |
| Safety Car & VSC strategy | On |
| Weather strategy | On |
| Teammate strategy coordination | On |
| Varied starting tyres | On |
| Race messages (HUD messages naming the drivers when a team makes a call) | **Off** |
| Team strategy styles | Varied |
| Debug logging | Off |

All settings apply live, without a rebuild.

---

## Compatibility and safety

- Works with custom grids, season addons and any race length: drivers, teams and race length are read from the
  game.
- On load the addon checks everything it uses against the running game's code. If anything doesn't match (a
  different game build, for example), it does nothing and the game's own strategy runs unchanged.
- Flashbacks, restarts, retirements and pausing are handled. Career data is saved only after a race finishes
  normally, and never inside the game's save.
