versions.changelog: - Works on EA's latest F1 25 update.

- Fixed: AI making a second safety car stop on tyres they had just fitted.
- Fixed: a missed safety car stop turning into a stop under green after the restart.

Now works with **Realistic Rain** addon.

- **Drying track: stay out for the change.** A car on wets (or intermediates) whose next planned stop is for the same or a wetter tyre now stays out while the track is drying, until it is ready for the next drier tyre, so that one stop becomes the tyre change instead of fresh wets now and inters a few laps later. The projection uses the last 90 seconds of drying, at most 20 minutes ahead. The hold only applies if the tyres will last (the same wear limit as finishing on a set). If the drying stalls, rain returns or wear climbs, the car goes back to its plan. At the stop, the game's weather call (or Realistic Rain's) picks the tyre.
- **Same wet/dry points as Realistic Rain.** The weather timing now uses the tyre crossover points of the game's own grip curves, which Realistic Rain calls the AI's tyres with: intermediates from 0.10 track wetness, full wets from 0.44. 1.2.0 used its own points (0.22, 0.12, 0.65 and 0.45), so it could time a weather stop the rain addon disagreed with.
- **Realistic Rain's "stay on wets" holds are respected.** Realistic Rain keeps AI cars out on wets by moving their stop past the finish while the track is too wet for the next, drier stint. Smarter AI Strategies used to write its own lap over that. Now a stop moved past the finish by anyone else is left alone for the rest of the stint, whether it is set before, between or during the game's strategy update. The addon's own "finish on these tyres" hold is not affected.

- New setting **Varied stop counts**. Before each race some AI cars with a one-stop plan are chosen to two-stop (bolder team styles more often, at most half the AI field, races of 16 laps or more).
- Two-stoppers plan their stops around a third and two thirds of the race, then use the usual undercut, cover, overcut and safety car tactics around those laps.

# MASSIVE UPDATE
---
### Adaptive Tyre Intelligence
- Learn directly from measured AI tyre wear during the race. The player's car is excluded.
- Accept full measured wear intervals in traffic at quarter of clean air weight rather than blocking collection.
- Blend compatible baseline, career and live evidence according to confidence, relevance, age and sample quality.
- Use learned wear and qualified age-dependent degradation estimates in existing race-time projections.
- Keep global baseline read-only during normal play. Save-specific tyre history requires verified save, season, round, circuit, compound, race distance and physics compatibility.
- Discard replayed/future observations after observed rewinds, retaining safe earlier history.
---
### Fixes and Safeguards
- Fix false Safety Car state remaining active after missed or replayed clearing notification. Reconcile game's instruction-checked stored deployment before planning - yield control when check state is unavailable.
- Recover cars returning from red flag garage parking after sustained on-track progress, without reviving confirmed DNFs.
- Correct fresh-set age handling and preserve previous compound when learning from a tyre change.
- Prefer staying out near the finish when observed rule compliance, measured wear, confidence and projected race time support it. *Wear above 75% is a risk the AI can accept, not an automatic pit threshold.*
- Preserve urgent game/other addon orders, mandatory compound checks and pit-loop guard.
- Validate participant list and fall back to independently checked live grid when supplied list is unusable.

- **Fixed: Team Orders' "Box This Lap" and "Stay Out" being cancelled.** Telling your team-mate to box early
  showed "Box overridden by strategy" in Team Orders. This addon also plans your team-mate's stops, and it put
  its own lap back over your order. Now, when anything else moves a car's stop to this lap or the next (a Team
  Orders order, or the game's own urgent stop), this addon leaves that stop alone until it is made, then plans
  the car's next stint as usual.
- Fixed infinite looping of pit stops and invisible tyre changes

### Fixed
- **AI cars pitting far too early.** Drivers could pit only about 7 laps into a stint after a fight ended, and
  whole queues of cars would stop early together. A stop could move up to 15% of the race earlier than planned
  (8 laps in a 50-lap race), however long the stint was.

### Changed
- **Undercuts are realistic:** an early stop is now 2 to 4 laps before the planned lap, depending on how long the
  stint is.
- **Early stops need a reason:** a car close ahead or behind, or a rival that has just pitted. Without one, a stop
  only moves earlier if it clearly saves race time.
- **Covers are limited:** a car can still answer a rival's stop this lap or the next, but not before 70% of its
  planned stint.
- **Late stops carry through:** if a stop runs late, the next stop moves with it, and the next stint (the last one
  included) keeps at least 70% of its planned length.

*Thanks to Alex and Cri for the report.*

addons.name: Realistic Rain
addons.author: Jonno
addons.summary: Rain that behaves like the real thing: showers drift across the circuit so one part is wet while another dries, the track soaks and dries with heat and traffic, standing water forms where the track floods, a dry line forms, wet kerbs and grass bite, and tyres aquaplane. A track panel tells you which tyre the track is ready for. Offline only.
addons.description:
# Realistic Rain

**Rain that behaves like the real thing.** Showers drift across the circuit, the track soaks and dries
patch by patch, a dry line appears as the rain eases, wet kerbs and grass bite, and tyres aquaplane when
it's too wet for them. The AI race in the same conditions.

---

## What it does

### 🌧️ Passing showers
Rain falls in showers about a kilometre across that drift over the circuit with the wind. One sector can be
soaked while another is already drying. You feel it in the grip, you see the rain build as you drive into
a shower, and the track surface around you looks as wet or dry as the patch you're on.

### 💧 A track that soaks and dries
Heavy rain floods the track in a couple of minutes, while drizzle only makes it damp. When the rain stops,
the track dries over several minutes: quicker on a hot day and with the whole field running, slower when
it's cold. Grip, spray, DRS and the safety car's weather rule all follow it.

### 🏁 A real dry line
As the rain eases, the cars clear the racing line before the rest of the track. Stay on it and you're
fine; put a wheel off-line and it's still wet. Fresh rain washes it away again.

### 🌊 Aquaplaning
Above a critical speed the tyre rides up on the water: no steering, no traction, and the brakes lock until
you slow down. It happens in standing water, or when the track is wetter than your tyre can clear:

| Tyre | Starts to float |
|---|---|
| Slicks on a wet track | about 100 km/h |
| Intermediates when it's too wet for them | about 180 km/h |
| Full wets | only in deep standing water, above about 250 km/h |

When each tyre is "too wet" comes from the game's own tyre data, so a tyre only floats once the game says
it's the wrong tyre. Pick the right one and you'll be fine.

### ⚠️ Slippery kerbs and grass
Wet painted kerbs and run-off lose a lot of grip, and grass is treacherous: drop a wheel on it at speed and
you can lose the car. If you do spin, you can always drive back off.

### 🌦️ Weather that changes gradually
Rain builds up and eases off over a few minutes instead of switching on and off, and comes in bursts and
lulls instead of one steady level. Flashbacks replay the same rain, and the forecast matches what falls.

### 🤖 The AI race in the same conditions
The AI feel the grip loss too, can aquaplane, and change tyres when the track is really ready, not when
the game's own weather curve says so.

### 📻 Track condition messages
Short notes in the game's own race notification: *Rain getting heavier*, *Standing water on track*, *Dry line
forming*, *Slick crossover approaching*.

---

## Settings

Everything can be adjusted on the addon's settings page:

- **Track wetness model:** Realistic / Balanced / Game
- **Drying speed:** 50–200 %
- **Dry racing line:** Realistic / Strong / Game
- **Rain variation:** Natural / Gentle / Stormy / Off
- **Weather changes:** Gradual / Very gradual / Game
- **Passing showers:** Scattered / Showery / Off
- **Local wet look:** on / off
- **Aquaplaning:** Mild / Realistic / Off
- **Slippery kerbs and grass:** Realistic / Extreme / Off
- **AI cars:** how much of the grip loss the AI feel (Half / Same as you / None)
- **Track condition messages:** on / off
- **Detailed logging:** for bug reports

**Want the full experience?** Set Aquaplaning to *Realistic*, AI cars to *Same as you* and Passing showers to
*Showery*.

---

## Good to know

- **Offline only.** Works in Grand Prix, Career, My Team, split screen and Story. Time Trial and online play
  are left exactly as the game ships them.
- **AI grip limit.** The game never lets an AI car's grip drop below 60%. With *AI cars* on Half or Same,
  Realistic Rain lifts that limit with a tiny game-code patch, only during offline races, and puts it back
  afterwards (and before any Time Trial session).
- **The sky is the game's.** Clouds and the forecast's weather types follow the game's own timeline; the
  addon shapes the rain and the water on the track.
- **AI racing lines** don't know about aquaplaning, so on the wrong tyres in heavy rain they may spin rather
  than lift. Turn *AI cars* down if that gets too much.
- **Works best with** dynamic or wet weather in a Grand Prix or career race.

addons.name: Contact Physics
addons.author: Kizi
addons.summary: What happens to a car in contact: rigid-body hits with mass, inertia, bounce, friction and rubbing tyres, wall scrapes, aero loss when sideways, damage, punctures. AI driving is in AI Driver Behaviour.
addons.description:
# Contact Physics

> **New in 0.8:** a clear split between the two addons.
> - **Contact Physics** is what happens to a **car**: contact, walls, aero, damage.
> - **AI Driver Behaviour** is how the AI **drives**: racecraft, slides and spins, reaction time.
>
> No setting is in both. The AI reaction time moved to AI Driver Behaviour, so **install AI Driver Behaviour 0.2.0 or newer with this version** to keep it.

> **Known limitations**
> - **Experimental.** The physics is tuned by test races, not proven. If something looks wrong, lower the strength or send the log.
> - **It can stop working after a game update.** It finds the game's contact code by its bytes. If a part can't be found, the log says "NOT installed" / "NOT found" and that part stays off. Nothing on disk is changed.
> - **Tested only in Grand Prix races** on the Steam build. Not tested in practice, qualifying, career or My Team.
> - **Energy-based wing damage** can be harsh with the game's high damage setting: a big hit can take a front wing off at once.
> - **Don't run it with the test addons** Contact Sim Light / Heavy (they use the same hook; the second one stays off).

## What is it?

In the game, a hit between two cars is softened a lot, only your car really gets pushed, walls bounce cars back like a pinball and a car sliding sideways keeps its full downforce. This addon makes contact behave like real physics:

- **Car to car:** the push comes from both cars' mass and inertia at the point where they touch, with bounce and friction. Off-centre hits turn cars, straight bumps push them, tyres that touch rub against each other and can launch a car. The same rules for your car, the AI, and AI against AI.
- **Walls:** cars scrape along a wall and lose speed, and barriers absorb most of a hit instead of throwing the car back.
- **Sideways:** a sliding or spinning car loses most of its downforce, like a real F1 car, so a spin slides further.
- **Damage:** hard hits damage the front wing by the energy of the hit, AI cars take the same damage as you, a hard tyre hit can puncture, and a car that flies can land with broken suspension.

Everything here is physics inside the game's own physics engine: nothing is scripted or animated.

## Settings

### Contact

- **Strength:** Normal (tuned values) or x1.5 / x2 / x3 for a stronger response.
- **Bounce:** how much cars bounce apart after a hit. Low, Medium or High. Gentle touches bounce more than high-speed hits.
- **Friction:** grip between the touching parts (tyre on tyre, bodies). Off, Low, Medium or High.
- **Tyre rotation:** rolling tyres rub in tyre-on-tyre touches, like real wheel-over-wheel contact.
- **Push AI cars:** on = AI cars take the push too and AI-AI touches count. Off = only your car (the game's own rule).
- **Game's own response:** Add = the game still pushes the cars apart, so hits cause damage (recommended). Ignore = ours only, no damage from car hits.
- **Applies to:** all touches (AI against AI too), or only touches with you.
- **Softening:** the game softens every car-to-car hit with two assists. Off = hits are not softened.

### Walls and aero

- **Wall physics:** cars scrape along walls and barriers absorb most of a hit's energy.
- **Aero loss when sideways:** Realistic = down to 30 % downforce when fully sideways, Strong = 12 %, Off = the game.

### Damage

- **Energy-based wing damage:** hard car-to-car hits add front-wing damage that grows with the speed squared. Off / Normal / High.
- **Equal damage for AI cars:** the game gives AI cars a different damage factor than yours. On = they take the same damage from a hit as you would.
- **Tyre punctures / punctures can hit you:** a hard hit at a tyre can puncture it (Rare, Sometimes, Often). AI only unless you turn the second option on.
- **Suspension after a jump / jump damage level / jumps can damage your car:** a car that flies and lands hard can get one corner damaged (or broken). AI only unless you turn the last option on.
- **Leave suspension to Terminal Damage:** if you also use Terminal Damage, this addon leaves suspension damage to it.

### Testing

- **Log contacts:** writes touches to the log. Leave it off.

All settings change live, no restart needed.

## Recommended settings (what we tested)

The defaults:

- Strength: Normal
- Bounce and friction: Medium
- Tyre rotation, push AI cars and wall physics: on
- Game's own response: Add
- Aero loss: Realistic
- Wing damage: Normal
- Equal damage: on
- Punctures and jump damage: Sometimes
- Softening: off

Tuning tips:
- If you want hits to look bigger, try strength x2.
- If cars get thrown around too much, go back to Normal or lower the friction.

## If something goes wrong

Send the log zip from the launcher (Send Logs). Please say which session type you used and which settings you changed.

## For the curious (technical)

Everything is memory only, nothing on disk.

**Car-to-car contact:** the game's contact code edits each contact record before the game's solver reads it. The addon finds it by byte patterns and adds a jump at its common exit. With "Add" the game's solver does the main push (so the game's damage system sees the hit). The addon adds bounce, friction and tyre rub from both car bodies' mass, inertia, velocity and contact point, applied with the game's own apply-impulse function on the physics thread (at most 4 pushes per car pair per physics step).

**Walls:** use the same records when one side is a barrier (not loose parts, cones or kerbs).

**Aero loss:** sets the game's own downforce multiplier per car through Swofty's live car fields, from each car's slip angle at 20 Hz.

**Damage:** writes the game's own wing, suspension and damage-factor fields. Punctures use the game's own puncture function.

**Cost:** about 0.1 - 2.5 ms per second of CPU time.

addons.name: AI Driver Behaviour
addons.author: Kizi
addons.summary: How AI drivers race and drive: gap to other cars, making room, how often they spin, how fast they react to slides and hits, damaged driving. Every driver can race differently. Experimental.
addons.description:
# AI Driver Behaviour

> **New in 0.2:** a clear split between the two addons.
> - **AI Driver Behaviour** is how the AI **drives**: racecraft, slides and spins, reaction time.
> - **Contact Physics** is what happens to a **car**: contact, walls, aero, damage.
>
> No setting is in both. The slide settings are now one **AI spins** choice, and the AI's reaction time moved here from Contact Physics. **Use Contact Physics 0.8.0 or newer** with this version.

> **Known limitations (noted by the author in testing, please read first)**
> - **Experimental.** We tested that the settings load and run. How much each one changes the racing is not measured.
> - **"Close racing: drivers differ" is a first version.** It changes values in the game's database that we only know from their names (how late a driver makes room, how far back they attack, how long they stay in a pass). The effect on track is not checked. It works on the game's own drivers; a driver added by a mod uses the plain values.
> - **The gap to other cars is the same for every car.** The game keeps it per team car, so it can't differ per driver.
> - **A closer, harder AI means more contact.** Use it together with Contact Physics if you want hits to matter.
> - Tested only in Grand Prix races on the Steam build 25251167.

## What is it?

The game's AI keeps a wide gap to other cars, catches every slide the moment it starts and never really loses the car. This addon lets you change that: race closer, hold the line longer, make mistakes on corner exit, react to slides and hits like a human, and sometimes spin.

It changes how the AI drives, not the physics: whether a slide becomes a spin is up to the game's physics.

## Settings

### Close racing

- **Gap to other cars:** the space an AI car leaves to the cars around it, most visible when racing side by side (the game's value is 0.35). Smaller = closer, wheel to wheel. None = no space kept. The same for every car.
- **When they make room:** whether an AI car gives room in a corner when another car is alongside (the game gives room at a third of a car, 0.33). Higher = it gives room later and holds its line.
- **Drivers differ:** gives each driver their own value around "when they make room", plus their own attack distance and commitment to a pass. Fixed per driver, the same every race. Small, Medium or Big sets how far apart the drivers are. Off = all drivers the same.

### Slides and spins

**AI spins** is one setting for how often AI cars slide and spin. It sets everything below together:

- **Stock:** all game behaviour. Exit mistakes, steering correction, traction control and lift off as in the game, lose the car at 23°, reacts to slides at once.
- **Some:** more exit mistakes, steering correction 75 %, traction control half, lifts off later, loses the car at the game's 23°, reacts to slides after 0.15 s.
- **More (default):** more exit mistakes, steering correction 75 %, traction control half, lifts off much later, loses the car sooner (17°), reacts to slides after 0.25 s.
- **Lots:** lots of exit mistakes, steering correction 50 %, traction control off, lifts off much later, loses the car much sooner (11°), reacts to slides after 0.4 s.
- **Custom:** uses the Custom spins settings below.

**Reaction: after a hit:** after a car-to-car hit the AI's steering stays where it was for a moment, so the hit can turn the car. Scales with the hit (0.1 s for a nudge up to 1.0 s for a big hit), or a fixed 0.2 / 0.4 / 0.6 s. Needs Contact Physics 0.8.0 or newer, which finds the hits.

### Custom spins

Only used when AI spins is Custom.

- **Exit mistakes:** throttle mistakes on corner exit: the AI gets on the throttle too early and the rear steps out. More = 30 % bigger, slides up to 32 degrees. Lots = 60 % bigger, up to 42 (the game allows 23).
- **Steering correction:** how hard the AI fights a slide: its steering gains at 75 or 50 %. The AI still turns into corners as fast as in the game.
- **Traction control:** the AI's traction control at half or off. Less = more wheelspin on corner exit.
- **When they lift off:** how far into a slide the AI starts lifting off the throttle (game 0.5). Higher = full throttle deeper into a slide.
- **When they lose the car:** the slide angle at which the AI gives up and spins (game 23 degrees). Smaller = it spins sooner.
- **Reaction to slides:** how long the AI's steering and throttle stay put when it starts to slide: Quick 0.15 s, Normal 0.25 s, Slow 0.4 s, or Off (the game).

### Damage

- **Speed with a damaged car:** how much a damaged AI car slows down for corners and braking. Pushing = half the game's slowdown, Flat out = a quarter. Both also raise the speed limit with a puncture.

### Pace

Removed in 0.1.7: it made the AI brake too late for corners on tight tracks such as Monaco. It may come back as a track-aware option.

### When changes apply

- **After a game restart:** Close racing, AI spins, Custom spins (except reaction to slides) and Damage.
- **At once:** Reaction after a hit and Custom spins: reaction to slides.

## Recommended settings (what we tested)

The defaults are a closer, harder AI than the game:

- Gap: Tight
- When they make room: Much later
- Drivers differ: Medium
- AI spins: More
- Reaction after a hit: Scales with the hit
- Damaged cars: Pushing

Tuning tips:
- If the AI spins too often, set AI spins to Some. If it never spins, try Lots.
- If the AI crashes into others too much, set "when they make room" to Later.

## If something goes wrong

Send the log zip from the launcher (Send Logs). Please say which session type you used and which settings you changed.

## For the curious (technical)

The Close racing, AI spins and Damage settings are about 27,600 database operations, each one switched by the addon's options.

**Per car** they set:
- `vehicle_buffer` (gap)
- the steering PID gains
- `exit_fallibility.max_yaw_angle_deg` (not on the safety cars)
- the traction control curve
- `lateral_traction_slip_angle_cut_in_proportion`
- `lost_control.angle`
- `damage_settings`

**Per driver** they set `alongside.min_presence_within_buffer` and `exit_fallibility.throttle_error_qualifying_race` (exit mistakes, every point x1.3 or x1.6, at most 1). With "drivers differ" on they also set `overtake.close_range_car_lengths_to_start_overtake` and `overtake.braking_zone_abort_overtake_time`.

Each driver's style is a number from -1 to 1 made from their database row name (the same every race). The "make room" value moves by 0.06, 0.12 or 0.18 times it, the attack distance by 15, 30 or 45 %, and the braking commitment by 20, 40 or 60 %.

**Reaction to slides and hits** is in memory: every AI car's controller gets a copy of its vtable whose update, while the driver "has not reacted yet", puts the held steering (and throttle) back. Slides are found from each car's slip angle at 20 Hz (above 7 degrees at 15 m/s). Hits come from Contact Physics through a function this addon's DLL exports.

## Credits

Made by Kizi. Thanks to Swofty for the launcher, the addon system and the live car operations.

# AI Driver Behaviour 0.2.0

Changes since 0.1.12.

> **Requires Contact Physics 0.8.0 or newer.** Install both together. The launcher refuses older Contact Physics versions, which had their own AI reaction settings.

## New

### Slides: AI spins
One setting for how often AI cars slide and spin.

- **Options:** Stock / Some / More / Lots / Custom (default: **More**)
- **Controls:** exit mistakes, steering correction, traction control, lift-off, give-up angle, and reaction to slides, all together.
- **No change if you never touched the slide settings:** *More* is exactly the old defaults.

### AI reaction to slides
The game's AI catches a slide the instant it starts, so it almost never spins. Now an AI car holds its steering and throttle briefly when a slide begins, like a driver who hasn't reacted yet. Most slides are still caught, but some become spins.

- **Some:** 0.15 s
- **More:** 0.25 s
- **Lots:** 0.4 s
- Each delay has a small random spread.

### Reaction: after a hit
Moved here from Contact Physics. Default: **Scales with the hit**.

After a car-to-car hit, the AI's steering stays put for **0.1 s** (a nudge) up to **1.0 s** (a big hit), so the hit can turn the car. Requires Contact Physics 0.8.0, which detects the hits.

## Changed

- The five slide settings are now named **"Custom spins: ..."**, and there is a new **"Custom spins: reaction to slides"**.
- These settings only apply when **AI spins** is set to **Custom**. Your old values are kept for when you pick Custom.

## Division of responsibility

From now on, no setting lives in both mods:

- **AI Driver Behaviour:** how the AI drives.
- **Contact Physics:** what happens to a car (contact, walls, aero, damage).

addons.name: PULSE
addons.author: Alex Sánchez
addons.summary: Feel the driver's heart: a heart rate that rises at the start, in a fight, after contact and under pressure, felt on screen (tunnel vision, heartbeat, G, impacts, fatigue) and shown on a bedside monitor, a TV biometrics card and a report.
addons.description:
Feel the driver's heart. Every driver gets a heart rate that lives with the race. It climbs on the grid, surges at lights out, rises in a fight, jumps after contact and comes down behind the safety car. You **feel** yours on screen and **see** it on a bedside monitor.

### The heart
- Worked out from what the car does, read from the game's memory (no UDP needed): the session, the start, the pace and the G, the nearest car (defending counts more than attacking) and what is at stake.
- Spikes of adrenaline from contact, spins and trips off the road, places lost and gained, track limits and penalties.
- The safety car, a red flag, the pit lane and the flag calm it. Fatigue builds over a long, hard race.
- Zones: CALM, FOCUSED, IN THE ZONE and the RED ZONE.

### On screen
- **Tunnel vision** in the red zone and a **heartbeat** throb at the edges.
- **G greyout** in fast corners and under hard braking.
- The **flash and blur** of an impact.
- **Fatigue** late in a long race.
- The centre of the picture always stays clear, and nothing shows while paused, in replays or in menus.

### Monitor, card and report
- A **bedside monitor** with the heart rate, the zone, a sweeping ECG trace and the stamina left. **F9** shows and hides it.
- In a race, a TV-style **DRIVER BIOMETRICS** card compares your heart with your rival's when you fight or touch.
- At the flag, a **PULSE REPORT**: your zone control score, your peak heart rate and what caused it, your average, the time in each zone and your stamina. It sits on the left by default, clear of the game's Driver of the Day.

### Settings
Find these in **ADDON SETTINGS**.
- Effects strength, a Comfort style (no throb, blur, flash or grain), Screen motion (Full, Reduced or Static), and each effect on its own.
- An optional key to switch the effects off and on while you drive.
- Where the monitor sits and how big it is, and its key.
- Where the report sits (left, right or centre), the card and the report.

### Works with
- Silly Season and Driver Momentum, at the same time.

### Credits
- PULSE: Alex Sánchez
- Swofty Launcher: Swofty

Unofficial fan addon, not affiliated with or endorsed by EA, Codemasters or Formula 1.

### Needs
Swofty Launcher 1.9.10 or later. Steam.

First version.

A heart for every driver, driven by what their car does: the start, pace and G, the car nearest them (defending counts more than attacking), what's at stake, and adrenaline spikes from contact, moments, places lost and gained, track limits and penalties. The safety car, a red flag, the pit lane and the flag calm it down, and fatigue builds over a long session. Four zones: CALM, FOCUSED, IN THE ZONE and RED ZONE.

Feel it on screen: tunnel vision, a heartbeat throb, G greyout under braking and in corners, the flash and blur of an impact, and fatigue. A strength slider, a Comfort style, Screen motion (Full, Reduced, Static), and every effect can be switched on or off on its own.

Medical monitor: heart rate, zone, a sweeping ECG trace and stamina, in the corner of your choice. F9 shows and hides it.

DRIVER BIOMETRICS card: your heart against your rival's, TV style, when you fight a car for a few seconds or make contact in a race.

PULSE REPORT at the flag: zone control score, your peak and what caused it, average, time in each zone, stamina and spikes. It sits on the left by default, clear of the game's Driver of the Day (Report position: left, right or centre).

Fair to the race: nothing counts while paused, a flashback takes back what happened after it, and a place given back within 30 seconds cancels out.

Tuned on real races in the game, so the numbers and the G match what F1 25 really gives.

Works without UDP telemetry.

addons.name: Improved Parc Ferme
addons.author: msyeett
addons.summary: Parc ferme like the real rule: change a locked setup row after qualifying and you start the race from the pit lane. Offline only.
addons.description:
Parc fermé the way it works in real F1. Got your setup wrong in qualifying? You can still fix it before the race, but it costs you: you start from the **pit lane**.

### How it works
- Parc fermé starts the moment you first leave the pits in **qualifying**.
- After that the **rear wing**, **suspension geometry**, **suspension**, **brake pressure** and **ballast** are locked by the rules.
- The setup screen doesn't grey them out any more. Change one and a message tells you which rows you changed.
- At the race start the game drives your car from its **garage** down the pit lane and stops it at the **pit exit**. The start lights wait until you stand there.
- You stay held at the pit exit while the field starts. A few seconds after the last car has passed, the pit exit opens and you join the race.
- On a track where the pit exit isn't known, your car waits in its garage instead and drives out once the field has passed.
- The pit lane start doesn't count as your pit stop.

### Still free
- Front wing, differential, brake bias, tyre pressures and fuel, like the real rule.

### Restarts
- Restart qualifying and parc fermé starts over.
- Restart the race and the pit lane start stays.
- Quit the game between qualifying and the race, or quit the race and load it again, and parc fermé is still there.

### Works with
- **Improved Car Setups** (0.1.0 or newer): its setup screen marks the locked rows and warns before you break parc fermé.

### Needs
- Swofty Launcher 1.8.36 or newer.
- A Grand Prix with qualifying on (Weekend Structure → Qualifying Format).
- Parc Fermé Rules on (Rules & Flags, on by default). With them off the addon does nothing.
- Offline sessions only, like all modded play.

### Credits
- Addon: msyeett
- Idea: Millo
- Swofty Launcher: Swofty

Unofficial fan addon, not affiliated with or endorsed by EA, Codemasters or Formula 1. Found a bug or something that looks off? Let me know on the Discord.

addons.name: AI Straight-line Nerf (EXPERIMENTAL)
addons.author: Kizi
addons.summary: EXPERIMENTAL, barely tested. Slows AI cars on straights: less ERS (stock cars, restart) + a live AI power and top-speed cut, mouse panel on F8. Use at your own risk.
addons.description:
# AI Straight-line Nerf

> [!WARNING]
> **EXPERIMENTAL.** This addon is barely tested. It may do nothing, behave differently on your setup, or break after a game or launcher update. Use it at your own risk.

Slows AI cars on the straights in F1 25 without making them slower in the corners.

## Requirements

- F1 25 on Steam, build **25251167** or newer
- Tested in Grand Prix races only

## What it does

AI cars in F1 25 are quick on the straights and never seem to run out of ERS. This addon cuts their ERS, power and top speed so they lose that edge.

## Settings

| Setting | Range | Effect | Applies |
|---|---|---|---|
| **AI ERS: stops deploying at battery** | 10% (stock), 25%, 40% | Battery level where the AI stops using ERS. A higher value means its battery runs dry sooner. | Needs a **game restart**. Game's own cars only. |
| **AI engine power cut (%)** | 0–10 | Takes power from every AI car. | **Live**. All AI cars, modded included. |
| **AI top speed cut (rpm)** | 0–600 | Cuts AI engine torque this many rpm under the limiter, which caps speed at the end of long straights. | **Live**. All AI cars, modded included. |
| **Open the panel when the game is paused** | On / Off | Opens the mouse panel on pause. | Off by default. |

## Mouse panel

Press **F8** in a session to open a panel with two sliders (power cut and top speed cut) and a Reset button.

- Drag the sliders with the mouse.
- Close it with **Esc**, the **X**, or **F8**.
- While it is open, the panel holds the mouse and the game gets none of your keys. Close it before you unpause.
- Values set in the panel are **not saved**. The launcher's settings load again at the next start.
- Needs Swofty's overlay.

## Your car

The cuts apply to a car while the AI drives it (for example with AI Drive). They are released when you take it back.

## Known limits

- **Not really measured:** the effect on gaps on the straights. I only confirmed that the settings load and the power cut is applied. The log shows `[ai-straight-nerf] 23 AI car(s): power -2%`.
- **ERS option:** it is a game database edit, so it only covers the game's own cars (2025/2026 cars, classics, older seasons, F2). Cars added by other mods keep the game's ERS values. We also do not know how much the AI's battery matters in the game's own AI.
- **Corner exits:** a cut also slows the AI there. Corner speed itself is untouched, because the AI plans it from grip, not power.

addons.name: Custom Sponsor Logos - Base Files
addons.author: JonnieDesigns
addons.summary: Base Files for sponsor addons made with AlterEgo. Contains no logos
addons.description:
Sponsor Base is the shared foundation for sponsor addons made with **AlterEgo** (coming soon). It adds no logos on its own. The sponsor addons that need it bring their own logos and rules.

You normally don't install it yourself: installing a sponsor addon from the Addon Browser installs Sponsor Base with it.

## What it does in My Team

- **Fixed sponsors** – FIA and Pirelli decals (see F1 Stickers Extension) locked on your car, but without income. They are added to your saved livery when the career loads.
- **Engine supplier sponsors** – logos that only appear for your engine supplier and are removed when you change supplier.
- **Emblems** – emblem stickers that are listed only while your team badge uses that emblem.

## Why a separate addon

Everything that depends on the game version lives here. After a game update only Sponsor Base needs an update, and your sponsor addons keep working.

Sponsor Base runs code in the game, which the fixed sponsor, engine sponsor and emblem features need. Keep it installed and switched on for as long as you use any AlterEgo sponsor addons.

Fixes Team HQ's vehicle performance comparison. A team that is not on that season's grid no longer shows up in it (Haas in 2015, Cadillac from 2017 to 2025), in the full list, the top three or the teams around you. The bars now show the real gaps between the teams: the slowest team's bar was almost empty (Manor at 40 against Mercedes' 304 in 2015), and now every percent of lap time a team was off the pace takes about 9% off the leader's bar, so 2015's Manor shows about 40% of Mercedes' bar. The order and the team rankings stay the same, and Hybrid's upgrade previews still show.

Progressive Career now starts careers from 2016, 2017 or 2018, with Manor as the eleventh team in 2016.
Fixes wrong line-ups: real drivers of the SWOFTY seasons no longer lose their seats to fill-in drivers, and your driver now races beside his real teammate instead of pushing him out.

addons.summary: Replace My Team and Grid liveries with your own full-colour designs. Includes a built in editor.
addons.description:
# Livery Editor

A Swofty Launcher addon for F1 25 that replaces My Team liveries, and the 2025 and 2026 grid team cars, with your own full-colour designs. Create **your own** liveries using the Livery Editor.

Once installed a **Livery Editor** tab appears in the sidebar.

## Use

The page has a tab for each season's car, **2025** and **2026**, each split into two sub tabs of MyTeam and Grid.

**MyTeam**: Every My Team livery you can pick in game.

**Grid**: The real teams' cars on that season's grid.

Each car is a card with a picture of it. A search box above the cards finds a livery by name.

### Ways to make a design:

- **Paint / Edit:** opens the editor on that car, where you paint it in 3D or on the flat texture sheet.
- **Use a Texture PNG…:** sets a finished 4096×4096 texture straight from a file. It opens in the editor on its own **Imported** layer, with the base hidden, so you can keep working on it.
- **Stock:** removes your design for that car and brings the stock livery back.

Then everything gets built on **next launch**. Your designs stay in the addon's data folder, so they survive launcher and addon updates.

## The editor

Paint straight onto the 3D car, or onto the texture sheet beside it. Drag to orbit, right-drag to pan, scroll to zoom.

**Tools**

- **Select (V)**: Pick, move, scale and turn items.
- **Eraser (X)**: Removes edited textures.
- **Brush (B)**: Freehand painting, with a **Smoothing** option for steadier strokes.
- **Paint Fill (U)**: Recolours a shape or stroke with your choosen colour.
- **Eyedropper (K)**: Picks up a colour from the car or the sheet.
- **Rectangle, Ellipse, Polygon (R, E, P)**: All shapes that can be drawn on the car.
- **Line (S)**: Draw a line, then drag its points to curve it.
- **Text (T)**: Add text to the body of the car.
- **Image (I)**: Add a PNG to be placed on the car.

**Editor**

- **Layers:** Add, remove, merge, hide, lock and mirror layers.
- **Materials:** Gloss, Satin, Matte, Metallic or Chrome similar to the in-game materials.
- **Restore stock:** Clears every layer and edit and goes back to the stock design in the game's default colours.
- **Export Texture PNG:** Saves the 4096×4096 picture as a file.

## Tips

- Textures are 4096×4096. A PNG of another size is turned down by the importer.
- A texture is made for one car's layout: a 2025 texture won't line up on the 2026 car.
- **Reset layout** puts the panels and toolbar back where they started. The panels and toolbar can be dragged to other edges.

## Conflicts

Other addons that replace the same livery or team textures change the same files. If both change the same car, the one later in the load order wins.

## Requirements

- Swofty Launcher with addon pages and build support.
- Windows or Linux (Steam Deck included).

This addon allows you to assign a helmet to each team. When an AI driver signs to that team, they will switch to that helmet automatically. You can use helmets that already exist in the game's database, or upload your own. There is also my team functionality, so you can assign your team's drivers each their own custom helmet through the my team tab.

addons.description:
# Circuit de la Sarthe (Le Mans 24H) for F1 25

Experience the legendary Circuit de la Sarthe, home of the 24 Hours of Le Mans, in F1 25!

This mod brings the full modern Le Mans circuit to the game as a standalone Swofty Launcher addon, featuring the iconic Mulsanne Straight, its two chicanes, Indianapolis, Arnage, and the high-speed Porsche Curves.

At approximately 13.6 km long, Le Mans offers a unique driving experience unlike any traditional Formula 1 circuit, combining extremely long straights with challenging braking zones and technical corners.

The mod is actively developed, with ongoing improvements based on community feedback.

## Features

- Full modern Circuit de la Sarthe layout (approximately 13.6 km)
- Both Mulsanne Straight chicanes
- Custom track geometry and elevation
- Reworked road, kerb, runoff and barrier collisions
- Custom AI racing lines and track data
- AI opponents and race session support
- Pit lane, garage and starting grid positions
- 60 km/h pit lane speed limit
- 2025 tyre compounds: C4, C5 and C6
- Le Mans-specific ERS settings for supported cars
- Updated DRS and Straight Mode zones
- Custom opening cameras and podium location
- Standalone Swofty Launcher addon
- Does not replace any original F1 25 circuit

## Latest Update — Version 1.0.4

Version 1.0.4 focuses on improving AI racing behavior, adapting energy deployment to the unusually long Le Mans circuit, and refining several gameplay and presentation elements.

**AI Improvements**
- Smoothed AI racing lines through Tertre Rouge and both Mulsanne chicanes.
- Removed fixed-speed braking triggers that caused excessively early braking at the chicanes.
- Retuned AI pace for 2025 and 2026 cars to improve racing behavior and consistency.

**ERS Improvements**
- Added a Le Mans-specific ERS adjustment, enabled by default under **Addon Settings → Le Mans Addon**.
- Increased per-lap ERS deployment limits for supported cars:
  - 2016–2025 cars: 16 MJ
  - 2026 cars: 26 MJ
  - 2012 KERS cars: 1.6 MJ
- Increased per-lap energy recovery limits by 4× for supported pre-2026 cars.
- Existing non-default energy limits are preserved.
- These adjustments apply only to Le Mans and can be disabled in the addon settings.

**DRS & Straight Mode**
- Extended the activation zone at the exit of Turn 27 by approximately 190 metres.
- Updated detection points, track markings and minimap indicators.

**Track & Presentation**
- Improved asphalt texture clarity around the pit boxes.
- Refined starting grid markings.
- Added chequered finish line markings on the main straight and in the pit lane.
- Updated opening cameras to showcase the start/finish straight and pit complex.
- Relocated the podium beside the finish line.

**Stability**
- Fixed an issue that could cause the game to freeze or crash at the end of the first lap.
- Added a native DLL to support Le Mans-specific ERS adjustments and a replay-related crash fix.

These improvements aim to provide a more enjoyable racing experience while addressing issues reported in previous versions.

Further refinements are still needed, particularly in AI behavior, track boundaries and overall performance.

## Upcoming Version 1.0.5 — AI, Track Boundaries & Performance

Based on continued development and community feedback, **Version 1.0.5 will focus on further improving AI behavior, refining track boundaries, and optimizing overall gameplay smoothness.**

Planned improvements include:

- **AI Racing Behavior:** Further refine racing lines, braking points and cornering behavior to reduce unexpected slowdowns, off-track excursions and collisions.
- **AI Consistency:** Improve AI pace and reliability across different corners and race conditions, especially during multi-car races.
- **Track Boundaries:** Review and refine track limits, runoff areas and vehicle tracking boundaries to prevent incorrect resets and unexpected off-track behavior.
- **Performance Optimization:** Optimize track assets and other performance-sensitive elements to improve frame rates, reduce potential stuttering and provide a smoother driving experience.
- **Race Stability:** Continue investigating and addressing issues affecting longer races and AI interactions.

The primary goal of Version 1.0.5 is to make Le Mans more reliable, consistent and enjoyable in full race sessions, while improving performance without unnecessarily sacrificing visual quality.

Additional fixes and improvements may be included as development continues.

## Known Issues & Limitations

This mod is still under active development.

- AI behavior may remain inconsistent at certain corners and during multi-car races.
- Some track boundaries and runoff areas may still require further refinement.
- Performance may vary depending on hardware and game settings, particularly during larger race sessions.
- Certain trackside scenery, textures and visual details may still require additional improvements.

These areas will continue to be addressed in future updates, with AI, track boundaries and performance taking priority in Version 1.0.5.

## Feedback & Support

Thank you to everyone who has downloaded, tested and reviewed this mod!

Your feedback has been extremely helpful in identifying issues and improving each release.

If you encounter any bugs, please leave a review or comment with details about the location, game mode and circumstances. Screenshots or short videos are especially helpful, particularly for AI-related issues and performance problems.

**The native DLL adjusts the per-lap ERS deployment and recovery limits specifically for Le Mans and includes a replay-related crash fix. The ERS adjustment can be turned off in Addon Settings and does not change energy limits on other circuits.**

**Thank you for your continued support and patience. Enjoy racing at Le Mans!**

Feedback: https://www.overtake.gg/downloads/circuit-de-la-sarthe-le-mans-24h-for-f1-25-swofty.88513/

addons.name: Driver Form
addons.author: msyeett
addons.summary: AI drivers have a weekend form: some are flying, others drift off the pace and make mistakes. Offline only. To see who is in form, turn on the toasts and Messages in ADDON SETTINGS. They are off by default.
addons.description:
Every AI driver in **Grand Prix**, **Driver Career** and **My Team** gets a form for the weekend. It carries through practice, qualifying and the race, so the running order stops playing out the same every time. Works with 2025 and 2026 cars.

### Form
- A third of the grid is in form, a third is out of form, and the rest are neutral.
- The form lasts the whole weekend, even if you close the game between sessions. A new track gives new forms.
- Your own car is never touched.

### In form
- Quicker over a lap, using the game's own AI pace rather than a power or grip boost.
- Hot spells of 20 to 60 seconds where they find extra time.
- Harder to pass: they start defending from further back.

### Out of form
- Slower over a lap.
- They brake earlier, carry less speed through corners and get on the throttle later.
- Bad patches of 20 to 60 seconds where they lose more time.
- Short mistakes of 3 to 8 seconds where they suddenly drop off the pace.

### Real driver gaps
- Optional: team-mates are as far apart as in real qualifying. Alonso is about 0.35 s quicker than Stroll, Sainz
  about 0.2 s quicker than Albon, Norris and Piastri almost level.
- Uses the 2026 averages, or the 2025 ones when the grid is the 2025 line-up. Other drivers keep the game's pace.
- Only team-mates move apart: the car's speed stays the game's. Works with Form strength Off too.

### Settings
Find these in **ADDON SETTINGS**. Everything you can see on screen is off by default, so out of the box the AI simply behaves differently.

- **Form strength**: Off, Subtle (about 0.8 s a lap either way), Normal (1.5 s), Wild (2.2 s) or Chaos (3.5 s). Normal is the default.
- **Real driver gaps**: team-mates as far apart as in real qualifying. Off by default.
- **Bad patches and mistakes**: on or off.
- **In form / Out of form toasts**: name the drivers to watch after the first lap.
- **Messages: Practice**, **Qualifying** and **Race**: how often notifications can appear, from None to Ultra.
- **Show mistakes**, **struggling**, **on a charge**, **place changes** and **pit stops**: pick the notifications you want.

### Needs
- Swofty Launcher 1.8.36 or newer.
- Offline sessions only, like all modded play.

### Credits
- Addon: msyeett
- Swofty Launcher: Swofty

Unofficial fan addon, not affiliated with or endorsed by EA, Codemasters or Formula 1. Found a bug or something that looks off? Let me know on the Discord.

addons.author: Swofty
addons.summary: Makes the MFD fuel mix a real choice: Lean saves fuel but loses power and runs hotter, Rich and Max add power for a lot more fuel. Applies to stock 2025 and 2026 and Swofty seasons; other addons opt in. Time Trial stays stock.
addons.description:
# Rich Fuel Mix

The MFD fuel mix becomes a real choice, as on the period cockpit dial.

- **Lean:** less fuel, less power, a hotter engine.
- **Standard:** the car as it is.
- **Rich:** more power for much more fuel. Starts, overtaking, defending.
- **Max:** the game's top mix. The richest map.

Requires Swofty Launcher 1.7.27 or newer. Keeping the chosen mix at a qualifying lap start needs 1.8.28 or newer; older launchers load the addon without it.

## Where it applies

The mixes apply to the stock 2025 and 2026 Grand Prix and Career and to every Swofty season: Classic Seasons 2016 to 2024 and Progressive Career. The **Stock 2025** and **Stock 2026** options turn the stock seasons off. Other addons opt their boxes and careers in.

Time Trial always runs the game's own fuel tables.

addons.name: Career Mode Editor
addons.author: Swofty
addons.summary: Edit a running career from the launcher: cash, resource points, R&D, driver ratings, the calendar and the weather, in My Team and Driver Career, with backups and undo.
addons.description:
Edit your career live while F1 25 is running, in **My Team** and **Driver Career**. Load into a career save, then open the **Career Editor** page in the launcher.

### How it works
- A live status shows whether the game is running, which career is loaded, the season and round, and whether edits can apply right now.
- Edits made while the game is loading or advancing time wait, then apply on their own once you're back in the hub.
- Every edit is recorded with its before and after values, with one-click undo in **History**.
- Your saves are backed up before the first edit of each session, and you can restore a backup from the launcher.
- Edits go through the game's own systems, and the game saves them like normal progress.
- Works on Windows and on Linux with Proton.

### Team and money
- Set or add Resource Points: your driver's wallet in Driver Career, the team's in My Team.
- Set or add cash, and renown, which triggers the game's own tier rewards (My Team).
- Add loyalty to your primary sponsor (My Team).
- See spending against the cost cap and refund expenses (My Team).
- Finish facility builds instantly, set facility levels, and buy and complete upgrades instantly (My Team).

### Drivers
- Edit any driver's ratings, AI or yourself: experience, racecraft, awareness, pace and focus.
- Swap seats mid-season between drivers on different teams; the car, livery and seat move with them.
- Sign free agents into a race seat in Driver Career; the driver they replace is released the way the game does it.
- Promote reserves and edit contract money: salary, signing bonus and performance bonuses (My Team).
- See the history of every driver move.

### R&D
- Complete upgrades instantly: one, a whole department, or everything.
- Fit, unlock, refund or reset upgrades.
- See every team's R&D progress, including each AI team's full tree.

### Season
- Reorder the calendar, remove a round, or add one from the tracks in your championship, in My Team and Driver Career (Progressive included). Rounds that haven't started can move; the sessions of every moved weekend stay in order.
- Sprint weekend changes (turning a round into a sprint weekend or back) are paused in 0.4.5; every round runs the game's own format, and choices you saved earlier are kept for when they come back.
- Replace a round's track, including with modded tracks.
- Add or take away championship points for any driver. Adjustments are kept and re-applied whenever the game rebuilds the standings, and the constructors' table follows along.

### Weather
- Plan the weather for each session the weekend runs, from practice to the race. On a sprint weekend the page names the Sprint and the Grand Prix.
- Choose when it changes: by lap in the race, by minute, or by how far into the session.
- Pick the state, from clear to storm, its intensity, and how quickly it rolls in.
- Lock the weather seed so a weekend's random weather stays the same, reroll it, or unlock it.

addons.name: Terminal Damage
addons.author: nyannoying
addons.summary: Beta. A broken car is no longer taken away: limp on, pull over or bring it in. Realistic failures with warning signs, a damage HUD, engineer radio, FIA rules, garage repairs and presets. Experimental and off by default: suspension damage from hits.
addons.description:
## Keep your broken car

When your car breaks, F1 25 normally takes it away from you on the spot. With Terminal Damage you keep it and deal with the failure like a real driver: limp on, pull over or bring it to your box. On top of that come realistic mechanical failures with warning signs, a damage HUD, engineer radio calls, FIA rules and garage repairs.

### Quick start

1. Steam version of F1 25 with Swofty Launcher 1.8.36 or newer. Install Terminal Damage from the Addon Browser, then restart the game.
2. In the game's own settings (Damage Settings) put **Car Damage** and **Car Damage Rate** on **Simulation** (see Game settings below).
3. A one-time message on the main menu points you to the preset. **Realistic** is the default: nothing else to set up.
4. Want it easier or harder? In the game: ADDON SETTINGS, Terminal Damage, **Preset**. Every option has a description there.
5. Optional: **Suspension damage from hits** is experimental and off by default (see below).

The game's UDP telemetry is not needed: SimHub, CrewChief and other telemetry apps keep port 20777. Made for offline sessions; you can load straight into a race.

### Game settings

Terminal Damage is built and tested with the game's own damage on **Simulation**. These two options are in the game's settings (Damage Settings), not in ADDON SETTINGS:

- **Car Damage: Simulation.** The game decides how much damage a crash does, and the limping, the broken corners, STOP THE CAR and the terminal damage rules all work on that damage. With Off there is no crash damage, so none of it can happen.
- **Car Damage Rate: Simulation.** How fast damage builds up.
- Reduced and Standard are not tested. If you use them and something looks wrong, tell me what you set.
- The random failures of *Mechanical failures in Grand Prix* are the addon's own (Realistic is the default). They come in races and sprints, not in practice or qualifying; the *Failure season* sets the real rates they follow.
- **Player Faults (Fault Frequency, Fault Types)** are on the same page. Leave them as they are: Off and Low work. In Career the addon ignores them, because it plans your failures and faults itself. In Grand Prix and custom races Off is the cleanest, since a higher Fault Frequency lets the game add its own faults on top of yours.

### New in 0.76

- **Suspension damage, rebuilt** (experimental option): how hard you hit decides it, no dice or timers. A light hit bends a corner, a medium one damages it (kerbs can then crack it), a heavy one breaks it, a very heavy one rips the wheel off. Nose and wing crashes count too (see Suspension damage from hits).
- **New option *Suspension strength*:** Forgiving, Realistic (default) or Brutal.
- **Race, broken corner (with suspension damage on): box, box.** Drive slowly into the pits this lap or the next instead of stopping within 20 seconds.
- **Flashback after a crash in the pit lane:** a crash at the pit entry no longer blocks Instant Replay and flashbacks.
- **Damage panel, new look:** a glass panel with rounded tiles and a coloured label under each part (see The HUD).

### New in 0.75.14

- **Attempt: no warnings in the Career weekend menu:** the failure clock waits until your car moves, so no CAR WARNING or radio call comes before the race.
- **Attempt: works together with Cool-down Lap:** no failure or pit call on the cool-down lap after the flag, and the cars it parks in parc ferme are left alone.

### New in 0.75.11

- **End Session in practice and qualifying:** ends the session at once again, as in the game.
- **Attempt: engine sound in the race replay:** your car should have its engine sound again in the replay after a retirement.

### New in 0.75 beta

- **Presets:** Casual, Realistic (default) or Hardcore set the main options at once.
- **Realistic mechanical failures**, now on by default in Grand Prix and custom races: the real failure rate of the season you pick (2012-2026), often with warning signs first. AI cars break down too.
- **Damage status panel:** a new HUD panel at the top right shows what is wrong with your car (see The HUD).
- **Engineer radio:** your engineer calls out warning signs, failures, brake problems and broken corners with the game's own voice lines.
- **Crashes:** one broken corner, front or rear, may let the car crawl on; heavy aero or body damage keeps the drive and calls you in; the messages name the broken corner.
- **More FIA rules:** in a race a car on a broken corner must stop; after a scripted failure or heavy damage, pit by the end of the next lap or retire.
- **Garage repairs** in practice and qualifying count down properly, and a withdrawn car says so.
- **Suspension damage from hits:** new, experimental and off by default.
- Many fixes, among them flashbacks after heavy damage, the replay sound after a retirement and race restarts. Full list in the [changelog](https://github.com/nyannoying1337/f1-25-terminal-damage/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

**Updating from 0.51.85:** the defaults are now the Realistic preset, so *Mechanical failures in Grand Prix* is **Realistic** (was Off) unless you set it yourself. Options you changed before stay as they are, and the preset then shows Custom.

### Presets

- **Casual:** no random failures in Grand Prix, 50 % power with a broken turbo or ERS part, the damage panel always on, the game's own red flag rules, a missed pit call means retired instead of disqualified, pause menu Retire ends your race at once.
- **Realistic (default):** real failure rates for the season, 30 % power, FIA red flag rules, disqualified for a missed pit call, damage panel on Auto, pause menu Retire asks you to pull over first.
- **Hardcore:** Realistic with 20 % power and no damage panel.
- **Custom:** change one of these options yourself and the preset shows Custom.

Picked in the game: reopen ADDON SETTINGS to see the changed options. Picked in the launcher: it applies at the next game start. All three presets also switch *Keep control after terminal damage*, *Keep control after a scripted failure* and *Engineer radio for damage and failures* on. A preset never changes hotkeys, the failure season, wheel physics, the engine sound, suspension damage or debug options.

### The HUD

Picture: [the damage panel, its colours and examples](https://github.com/nyannoying1337/f1-25-terminal-damage/blob/main/docs/damage-panel.png)

**Damage status panel** (option *Damage status panel*): tiles at the top right of the race HUD, under the lap times. The header shows CAR and the worst state: OK, CHECK (yellow), WARNING (orange) or FAILURE (red); from orange on, the panel's edge glows in that colour.

- **Six tiles:** engine, ERS, gearbox, brakes, suspension and power, each coloured by how bad it is.
- **Yellow:** an early sign, such as a gearbox starting to wear, or a bent corner.
- **Orange:** a fault is active: less power, slow shifts, a lost gear, brake trouble or a weakened corner.
- **Red:** the part is out, a corner is broken, or you are limping.
- **The label under a tile:** OUT (failed), -15% (power lost), CUTS (power cutting in and out), x6 (shifts 6 times slower), NO 3 (3rd gear lost), -40% (rear braking lost; + means the rear brakes grab), FL, FRONT or ALL (which corners), LIMP (crawling on a broken corner).
- **Auto** (default) shows only the tiles with a problem, so nothing is shown while all is fine. **Always on track** shows all six, **Off** none. The panel goes away once your race is over.

**Messages** in the middle of the screen tell you what happened and what to do next: SUSPENSION DAMAGE, BROKEN FRONT CORNER, WHEEL LOST, MECHANICAL FAILURE, BRAKE FAILURE, HEAVY DAMAGE, STOP THE CAR, BOX BOX, DISQUALIFIED, CAR WITHDRAWN, CORNER REPAIR, CAR REPAIRED and more. Messages titled ENGINEER give advice, for example "the rear brakes are grabbing, bias forward".

**Engineer radio** (option *Engineer radio for damage and failures*): the same events as voice calls. Off: only the messages stay.

**Damage MFD page:** with the experimental suspension damage on, the game's own damage page shows the damaged corners (the stock page shows them as tyre wear).

### What happens when something breaks

- **Engine (ICE) or gearbox:** no drive; the car rolls out.
- **Turbo, MGU-K, MGU-H, battery or control electronics:** reduced power (30 % throttle in Realistic; option *Power with a broken turbo/ERS part*).
- **A crash that breaks a corner:** the car usually cannot be driven. With **one** broken corner it may still crawl on with about a third of its power: a collapsed suspension 85 % at the front and 60 % at the rear, a front wheel coming loose 35 %. Never once the game tears the wheel off: that also stops the engine.
- **Race, crawling on a broken corner:** STOP THE CAR. Pull over as soon as it is safe, or get to the pit lane. After 20 s of driving on track the car retires as unsafe. With *Suspension damage from hits* on: BOX, BOX instead. Drive slowly into the pits this lap or the next; the crew pushes the car into the garage and your race ends there. Stay out longer and the car retires.
- **Practice and qualifying, crawling on a broken corner:** bring it back to the garage for a rebuild.
- **Heavy aero or body damage** that the game calls terminal (front wing, sidepods, floor, rear wing, diffuser): the car keeps its drive. Race: pit by the end of the next lap or retire. Practice and qualifying: back to the garage, out for the session.
- **Engine sound:** a failed engine goes silent at once; after terminal crash damage the engine dies after 3-6 s; a broken car standing still switches off after 6 s.
- Your stopped car brings out no safety car or red flag.

### Realistic failures (Grand Prix, custom races and Career)

- *Mechanical failures in Grand Prix*: **Realistic** (default) uses the real failure rate of the season in *Failure season* (2012-2026; pick your car mod's season). Short races have fewer failures, and practice and qualifying none. Also: a fixed chance (10-50 %) or Off.
- Many failures give **warning signs** first: power loss, cut-outs, slow or rough shifts, a lost gear, rear brake trouble. **Lift and coast** to nurse the part: it lasts longer.
- Some faults stay partial: slow shifts, a missing or jammed gear, DRS, ERS or lean fuel trouble, a rear brake-by-wire fault (from 2014).
- AI cars break down at the season's rate too.
- **Each team has its own rate** (new in 0.75.6): a team's cars break down as often as that team's did in the season, from its real retirements, so in 2026 an Aston Martin or a Cadillac fails far more often than a Mercedes (Cadillac about 1 race in 3.7 per car, Aston Martin about 1 in 2.6). The season's overall rate stays the same: the rates of the cars in your race add up to it, whichever teams are on the grid. A team's rate is pulled towards the season's average when its numbers are few, and in a year where the teams hardly differed (2023-2025, and so the default season 2025) the rates are nearly equal. A team the addon does not know gets the average. The log lists the teams it found and their rates. Every team in every season: [team failure factors](https://github.com/nyannoying1337/f1-25-terminal-damage/blob/main/docs/team-failure-factors.md).
- **Career R&D matters** (new in 0.75.6): every team starts a Career with the same five *Durability* upgrades done; each further finished one lowers that team's failure rate, up to half with all of them done. Early upgrades count most (new in 0.76.2): the first one takes almost 2 % off, the first third of them gives half of the effect, and the last ones add little. It counts for you and for the AI teams (the game researches theirs during the season), and only for the team that did the research: when you research, the AI cars do not get worse, and a grid that develops fails less as the season goes on. A research that fails does not count (the same upgrade can be started again). Option *R&D durability lowers failures (Career)*, on by default. At the start of a Career nothing changes.
- **Career and My Team** get them too (new in 0.75.5, experimental: only short tests so far): with Realistic on, they replace the game's own rolled failures and its temporary fault for your car, so the real team rates and the teams' Durability R&D decide who breaks down, not the game's own model. The AI cars keep the game's temporary faults.

### Retirement

- **Pull over:** stand still for 10 s, on track or stranded in the pit lane.
- **Your pit box (race):** no tyre stop; your crew pushes the car into the garage, then you retire.
- **Retire without damage:** radio menu Retire, pause menu Retire or Ctrl+Shift+F11, then pull over or box. The hotkey cancels the request while you are still on track.
- After retiring, the parked car stays where it is instead of the AI driving it away.
- **Flashbacks:** back before the damage, the car is whole again with full power.

### Red flags (FIA rules)

- A failed engine, power unit or gearbox, or a car left on track without drive: you retire.
- A car limping on one broken corner may be rebuilt during the red flag (80 % for a suspension, 50 % for a lost wheel) and take the restart. Heavy aero or body damage may be repaired too.

### Practice and qualifying

- Retiring would end the whole session, so your car goes back to its garage instead.
- **Limped in on a broken corner:** the team rebuilds it, 20-30 minutes for a suspension and 30-45 for a lost wheel. The game's repair timer counts down: wait, or use skip or fast forward (uses session time).
- **A damaged corner that still holds** (experimental suspension damage): 4-20 minutes, by how bad it is.
- **Did not make it back** (stopped on track, or Retire from Session): withdrawn for the rest of the session, ready again in the next one.
- **Engine or gearbox failure in Career:** the car stays in the garage until you fit a new part in the Power Unit menu.

### Career and My Team (experimental)

- Realistic failures work here too (see above). With the option on Off, the game's own failure chances and timing stay unchanged; a fixed chance adds to them.
- When the game would hand your car to the AI after a failure, you keep it: pit by the end of the next lap or retire, otherwise you are disqualified (or retired, see the options). A DSQ stays DSQ in the results.

### Suspension damage from hits (experimental, off by default)

Turn on *Suspension damage from hits (experimental)*, then restart the game.

- How hard you hit decides what happens, no dice and no timers. A light hit **bends** a corner (the car pulls to one side). A medium hit **damages** it; kerbs then wear a damaged corner down until it **cracks** and can break. A heavy hit **breaks** it: the car limps on that corner. A very heavy hit **rips the wheel off**.
- A hit on the nose, the front wing or the rear of the car reaches the nearest corners too. Scrapes, boards and normal kerbs do not break a healthy corner.
- *Suspension strength*: **Realistic** (default): a hit straight into a wall at about 25 km/h breaks a corner, about 45 km/h rips the wheel off. **Forgiving** takes more, **Brutal** takes less. Needs a game restart.
- The messages say what you feel and what to do: bent, damaged, cracked, broken.
- Shown on the damage panel and the game's damage MFD page; repaired in the practice and qualifying garage; undone by a flashback.
- **Using Heavier Damage?** They work together: while this option is on, the game's own suspension damage stays at stock on the cars it covers (your car; every car with the AI option), so Heavier Damage's *Suspension & wheel damage* does not add up with it. Heavier Damage's wing damage and its other settings stay.
- *Suspension damage for AI cars* is a separate experimental option.

### Something not working?

Every part has its own option. Turn off only the part that gives you trouble for now, keep the rest, and send me your log so I can fix it. Some options need a game restart; their description says so.

- **Random failures:** *Mechanical failures in Grand Prix*: Off.
- **Damage panel:** *Damage status panel*: Off.
- **Radio calls:** *Engineer radio for damage and failures*: off.
- **Suspension damage:** *Suspension damage from hits*: off (the default).
- **Retire in the menus:** *Retire in the radio menu* or *Retire in the pause menu: pull over first*: off.
- **Red flag rules:** *FIA red flag rules for a terminally damaged car*: off.
- **Career failures:** *Keep control after a scripted failure*: off.
- **Everything:** *Keep control after terminal damage*: off gives you the game's own behaviour.

**Your log:** loader.log in the newest folder of %LOCALAPPDATA%\Swofty\sessions (while the game runs: the swofty folder inside your F1 25 folder). Post it in the Terminal Damage discussion on [OverTake](https://www.overtake.gg/downloads/terminal-damage-beta.88096/) or open an issue on [GitHub](https://github.com/nyannoying1337/f1-25-terminal-damage/issues), and say what happened and roughly when: session type, track, flashback or restart.

### Other options

- **Player wheel behavior:** Stock (default), Reduced jolting (experimental) or Loose wheels. **Loose AI wheels** is separate and off. Restart the game after changing either.
- **Debug options** are at the bottom of the list and off. Leave them alone unless I ask you to test something.

### Known issues

- The Career R&D effect and its cap of half with every Durability upgrade done are a first guess: I will tune them once I have seen how fast the AI teams research.
- Suspension damage is experimental: its tuning can still change.
- Suspension damage: a hard landing (after a big kerb, or flying off the track) does not break a healthy corner yet.
- Career is not fully tested with the limping, red flag and garage repair rules yet. The realistic failures there (0.75.5) are new: one gearbox failure from the real rates has been seen in a Career race so far, and it played out as designed. An AI car that fails in Career stays where it stopped for up to two minutes before the game takes it to its garage.
- No safety car HUD while your car is terminally damaged: the game shows it only to cars it does not count as terminally damaged.
- A red flag during terminal damage can still cause AI or spectator camera issues.
- AI cars with terminal damage stand where they stopped until the game takes them to their garage: about 15 seconds after a crash, up to two minutes after a failure the addon planned. If the game never does (it happened after flashbacks), the addon puts the car in its garage after two minutes on track or 30 seconds in the pit lane, never during a safety car or red flag.
- A flashback during the box stop or the garage push is not fully tested in game.
- **Qualifying ICE replacement, Skip repairs and practice replacement timing: NOT TESTED, MIGHT BE BROKEN.**
- A game update can switch parts of the addon off until it is updated.

### Spectator addon integration

A versioned player-state interface lets spectator addons react to a confirmed retirement and recovery. Terminal Damage itself does not switch cameras. The integration documentation is in the GitHub repository.

### Code reuse

This release uses the [Terminal Damage Attribution License 1.0](https://github.com/nyannoying1337/f1-25-terminal-damage/blob/main/LICENSE), a custom license. Published mods/projects using substantial portions must visibly show **Uses work from Terminal Damage by nyannoying** and link to [Terminal Damage](https://github.com/nyannoying1337/f1-25-terminal-damage). Redistributed copies must retain the copyright and license notices. Earlier MIT releases keep their MIT terms; third-party SDK licenses are unchanged. See LICENSE for the complete terms.

# Terminal Damage 0.76.3 beta

# Terminal Damage 0.76.2 beta

The addon no longer contains any network code, and in Career early Durability upgrades now count more than late ones. Everything from 0.76.1 is in this release.

## Changed

- **Career R&D, Durability upgrades.** Every upgrade used to take the same 1 % off your team's failure rate. Now the first ones count most: the first upgrade takes almost 2 % off, the first third of them gives half of the effect, and the last ones add little. All of them done still halves the failure rate. Real cars got more reliable the same way: the big problems were fixed first.
- **No network code.** The debug option *UDP telemetry port* is removed, and with it the addon's only network code (a listener for the game's own telemetry on your PC, off by default). Nothing changes in the game: the addon reads your speed from the game itself.

Full notes: https://github.com/nyannoying1337/f1-25-terminal-damage/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

# Terminal Damage 0.76.1 beta

Each team's own failure rate works again, and the 2026 failure rates include the São Paulo Grand Prix. Everything from 0.76.0 is in this release.

## Fixed

- **Failures per team.** In Grand Prix and custom races the addon could not tell which team a car belongs to, so every car got the season's average failure chance. Each team's cars break down at that team's own rate again.

## Changed

- **2026 failure rates, now up to round 20 (São Paulo).** An average 2026 car fails in 12.5 % of Grands Prix (was 12.9 %). Battery failures come a little more often, and Aston Martin is still the team that breaks down most.

Full notes: https://github.com/nyannoying1337/f1-25-terminal-damage/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

# Terminal Damage 0.76.0 beta

Suspension damage is rebuilt: how hard you hit now decides whether a corner bends, cracks or breaks, with no dice and no timers. Flashbacks work after a crash in the pit lane, and the damage panel has a new look. Everything from 0.75.15 is in this release.

## Read this first

- **Updating from 0.75.15:** nothing to set up. *Suspension damage from hits* is still experimental and off by default. If you turn it on, the new *Suspension strength* option starts on Realistic.

## New

- **Suspension damage, rebuilt** (option *Suspension damage from hits*). What happens depends only on how hard you hit. A light hit **bends** a corner: the car pulls to one side, and you can drive on. A medium hit **damages** it: kerbs then wear it down, and it can **crack** and break. A heavy hit **breaks** it: the car limps on that corner. A very heavy hit **rips the wheel off**.
- **Nose and wing crashes count too.** A crash with the front or the rear of the car now reaches the nearest corners, not only a hit on a wheel.
- **New option: Suspension strength.** Realistic (default): a hit straight into a wall at about 25 km/h breaks a corner, about 45 km/h rips the wheel off. Forgiving takes more, Brutal takes less. Needs a game restart.
- **Race, broken corner: box, box.** With suspension damage on, a broken corner no longer means "stop the car within 20 seconds". Drive slowly into the pits this lap or the next. The crew pushes the car into the garage, and your race ends there. Stay out longer and the car retires.
- **Flashback after a crash in the pit lane.** A crash at the pit entry, where the pit speed limit shows, blocked Instant Replay and flashbacks, so you had to retire. Flashbacks work there now.
- **Plain messages.** The suspension messages and option texts say what you feel and what to do: bent, damaged, cracked, broken.
- **Damage panel, new look.** A glass panel with rounded tiles and a coloured label under each part. When something is badly damaged, the panel's edge glows in that colour.

## Known issues

- Suspension damage is still experimental, and its tuning can change.
- A hard landing (after a big kerb, or flying off the track) does not break a healthy corner yet.

Full notes: https://github.com/nyannoying1337/f1-25-terminal-damage/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

# Terminal Damage 0.75.15 beta

The addon's Swofty manifest now says that it supports the Steam version of F1 25 only and needs Swofty Launcher 1.8.36 or newer. Nothing changes in the game. Everything from 0.75.14 is in this release.

Full notes: https://github.com/nyannoying1337/f1-25-terminal-damage/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

# Terminal Damage 0.75.14 beta

Two attempted fixes: no car warnings in the Career weekend menu, and Terminal Damage works together with Cool-down Lap. Everything from 0.75.12 is in this release (0.75.13 was never released).

## New

- **Attempt: no failures or warning signs in the Career weekend menu.** After qualifying, the game loads the race behind the weekend menu with your car standing in it. The addon took that for racing: its failure clock ran in the menu, and a planned failure could show its warning signs (the CAR WARNING panel, the engineer's radio) before the race began. The failure clock now starts once your car moves.
- **Attempt: Cool-down Lap compatibility (issue #19).** Cool-down Lap (by vmknolle) lets you keep driving after the chequered flag and holds back the game's end-of-race hand-over of your car, which Terminal Damage uses to know your race is over. Depending on which addon hooked first, Terminal Damage could take the cool-down lap for racing: a planned failure or a pit call could still come. Cool-down Lap 0.38.8 and newer tell Terminal Damage when your race is over and which AI cars it parks in parc ferme; Terminal Damage stops its failures there and leaves those cars alone. Without Cool-down Lap nothing changes.

Full notes: https://github.com/nyannoying1337/f1-25-terminal-damage/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

# Terminal Damage 0.75.12 beta

The addon's Swofty manifest now names its source repository, as Swofty recommends for addons with native code. Nothing changes in the game. Everything from 0.75.11 is in this release.

Full notes: https://github.com/nyannoying1337/f1-25-terminal-damage/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

# Terminal Damage 0.75.11 beta

Two small fixes: End Session works again in practice and qualifying, and an attempt to bring back your car's engine sound in the race replay after a retirement. Everything from 0.75.10 is in this release.

## New

- **End Session works in practice and qualifying.** The game uses the same function for End Session there as for Retire in a race, and the addon turned it into a retirement: you were asked to pull over and the session went on. End Session now ends the session at once, as in the game. In a race, Retire in the pause menu still asks you to pull over or box first.
- **Attempt: engine sound in the race replay after a retirement.** The addon keeps a retired car's engine off through the retirement camera. When you watched the full race replay from the results, your car could stay silent in it. The sound now comes back once the game puts your car away after the race.
